definition: AA Coffee Grading refers to a size-based classification system for green coffee beans, primarily used in Kenya and other East African countries. The “AA” designation means beans of the largest size category, typically 7.2mm or larger in diameter [1] . This grading method sorts beans through screens with specific-sized holes, with larger beans generally associated with higher quality. In Kenya’s grading hierarchy, AA represents the premium classification, followed by grades like AB, PB ( peaberry ), and others [2] .

Acrid Coffee Taste refers to a specific and undesirable flavor defect in coffee. [1] It has a harsh, sharp, and irritating quality, which is characteristic of a burning or pungent bitterness. [2] This flaw is distinct from desirable acidity and indicates problems that can range from production and roasting to the brewing process itself. [3]

Adenosine (uh-DEN-uh-seen) is a naturally occurring purine nucleoside found in every cell of the human body, where it acts as a signaling molecule that regulates sleep, arousal, and cardiovascular function. [1] Though it belongs to biology rather than the roaster’s vocabulary, this compound explains much of how caffeine affects the brain. In coffee science, adenosine matters because caffeine produces its well-known alerting effect primarily by blocking adenosine receptors rather than by adding energy to the body. [2]

The Aerobie coffee maker is a manual brewing device that uses air pressure to extract coffee. It involves steeping ground coffee in hot water before using a plunger to force the liquid through a filter. The device consists of a cylindrical chamber, a plunger, and paper filters that remove sediment while allowing oils to pass through.

AeroPress refers to a manual coffee brewing device invented in 2005 by Alan Adler . It consists of a cylindrical chamber, a plunger with an airtight seal, and a filter cap. The method involves using manual air pressure to force steeped coffee through a micro-filter. It is known for producing a concentrated, smooth, and low-acidity coffee in 60 to 90 seconds. The result is a type of espresso-style concentrate that can be consumed as is or diluted into an Americano .

Affogato, from the Italian word meaning “drowned,” is a classic Italian dessert-beverage hybrid that consists of a scoop of vanilla gelato or ice cream over which a shot of hot espresso is poured [1] . This elegant creation occupies a unique position in coffee culture , straddling the line between dessert and coffee drink [2] .

African Civet ( Civettictis civetta ) is a large nocturnal mammal native to sub-Saharan Africa and the species most often cited when coffee is described as “African civet coffee.” [1] It is the second-largest civet species after the binturong, and it is omnivorous, eating everything from coffee cherries and invertebrates to small mammals and millipedes. [1]

Definition and Common Usage After Dinner Roast refers to a dark roast coffee made for consumption after meals. This roast style undergoes extended heating at temperatures between 370°F–540°F during the Maillard reaction, resulting in beans with a bold, rich flavor profile [1] . The intense roasting process reduces caffeine content somewhat compared to lighter roasts—a typical dark roast contains approximately 51 mg of caffeine per serving versus 60 mg in light roasts [1] .

Aftertaste in Coffee (also known as the finish ) refers to the lingering sensory impression of flavor , aroma, and mouthfeel that remains after swallowing. It has a role in indicating coffee quality and brewing precision. [1] This final impression can evolve, revealing deeper notes that are characteristic of the bean’s origin, processing method, and roast level.

Aftertastes—the lingering flavors and mouthfeel sensations post-sip—form coffee’s final impression, bridging initial taste to lasting memory. These residual notes, spanning sweet to ashy, emerge from bean origin, roast, and extraction. [1] Crucially, they expose what first sips may conceal: roast flaws, fading freshness, or brewing missteps. [2]

Aged Coffee refers to coffee produced by storing green, unroasted beans for an extended period, which can range from two to three years to much longer. [1] This process requires controlled conditions and is distinct from coffee that is stale or poorly stored. The managed storage helps develop a specific flavor profile. The resulting brew has earthy and pungent flavors, lower acidity , and increased body . [2]

Ageing, spelled as “aging” in American English, is the gradual accumulation of changes in an individual over the course of their life. In humans, this is a complex, multidimensional journey involving physical, psychological, and social transformation.

An air roaster, also known as a fluid bed roaster, is a coffee roasting machine that uses hot air as the primary heat transfer medium to roast coffee beans. The core principle involves suspending green coffee beans in a stream of heated air, creating a “fluid bed” where beans float and tumble continuously during the roasting process [1] .

Alan Adler is an American inventor. His inventions include aerodynamic toys, such as footballs with fins and flying rings and discs. His Aerobie Pro flying ring set several world records for the farthest thrown object. In 2005 he invented a coffee brewing device and method called the AeroPress . He has approximately 40 patents in electronics, optics, and aerodynamics.

Alkaline Taste in Coffee is a sensory term in coffee tasting describing a dry, chalky, or soapy sensation, distinct from true acidity or bitterness, primarily perceived at the back of the tongue. It is a key characteristic of many dark-roasted coffees and beans from specific regions like Indonesia. Despite the name, coffee is chemically acidic, with this taste arising from minerals and roasting byproducts.

Altura Coffee (from the Spanish word for ‘height’) refers to a designation for coffee beans cultivated at high altitudes, typically above 1,200 meters (4,000 feet). [1] This term is a quality marker for high-grown, often mountain-grown, coffee. It means beans that have matured slowly in cooler temperatures, a process that produces greater density and a more complex flavor profile. [2]

Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by memory loss, cognitive decline, and behavioral changes, primarily associated with the accumulation of amyloid-beta plaques and tau protein tangles in the brain. In some cases, early signs can appear as early as the mid-40s.

American Roast refers to a medium-level roast on the coffee spectrum, between lighter roasts (such as Cinnamon or Light) and darker varieties (like French or Italian) [1] . This roast level has beans with a rich brown color and lacks the oily surface seen in darker roasts [2] . American Roast strikes a balance in flavor, preserving some of the bean’s original characteristics while developing deeper caramelized notes.

Antestia bugs (Antestiopsis spp.), also known as variegated coffee bugs or shield bugs, are small insects belonging to the Pentatomidae family that feed on coffee plants. These pests pierce coffee cherries and beans with their mouthparts, causing physical damage and introducing harmful bacteria into the fruit [1] . The bacteria produce 2-isopropyl-3-methoxypyrazine (IMP) when beans are heated at high temperature , resulting in the distinctive potato taste defect (PTD) [2] .

Apaneca-Ilamatepec is a legally protected coffee-growing denomination of origin in western El Salvador, centered on a volcanic mountain range that includes the Santa Ana (Ilamatepec) volcano. Its high-altitude specialty coffees—shaped by volcanic soils and shade-grown farms—typically cup as sweet, balanced, and citrus- or chocolate-leaning. The region earned El Salvador’s first Denomination of Origin status in 2010, with European Union recognition following in 2012, and that legal framework anchors everything from farm practices to export labels. [1]

Arabian Mocha Coffee refers to a premium single-origin coffee variety cultivated in Yemen’s mountainous regions across the Arabian Peninsula [1] . This coffee has a medium to full body with bright acidity and a complex sensory profile [2] . The beans undergo dry processing, where they ferment inside the fruit, developing their signature taste characteristics [3] . The resulting cup has a rich, wine-like flavor with distinctive chocolatey undertones [1] .

Arabic coffee is a general name that refers to the two main ways coffee is prepared in many Arab countries: Turkish-style, and Saudi Coffee. The Turkish coffee brewing method is common in the Levant, but brewed without the addition of sugar. Cardamom is often added, or it is served plain قهوة سادة qahwah sādah (lit. “plain coffee”).

Artisan Coffee refers to coffee produced through a hands-on, craftsmanship-focused process. This approach is known for small-batch roasting , direct relationships with farmers, and meticulous attention to quality from cultivation to brewing . [1] It is a type of production within the specialty coffee movement, distinguished by its philosophy and production scale.

Arusha coffee takes its name from the Arusha region in northern Tanzania, where this Arabica variety has been cultivated since the colonial period. The variety emerged from French Mission Bourbon stock introduced to the area in the early 20th century, adapting to the volcanic soils and high-altitude conditions surrounding Mount Meru and Mount Kilimanjaro.

Ashy Coffee Definition and Sensory Profile Ashy coffee refers to beans with a burnt character reminiscent of cigarette ash or fireplace remnants. This negative flavor attribute results from excessive roasting , particularly when beans remain in a drum roaster beyond approximately 17 minutes, leading to burnt or baked flavors [1] . The ashy profile has a dry, powdery sensation on the palate, often accompanied by bitter , charcoal-like notes that overwhelm the coffee’s inherent qualities.

A civet is a small, slender mammal, most active at night, that inhabits the tropical forests of Asia and Africa. The term refers to over a dozen distinct species, with the greatest variety found in Southeast Asia. The most well-known of these is the African Civet, or *Civettictis civetta*. Historically, this animal was the main source of a powerful musky substance used in the creation of fine perfumes, giving it significant economic importance for centuries.

Aspiration in Coffee Tasting refers to a standardized sensory evaluation technique. [1] It involves a taster drawing brewed coffee into the mouth through vigorous, audible suction. The technique is a core component of professional coffee cupping protocols. [2] This method atomizes the liquid to coat the tongue evenly and releases aromatic vapors for retronasal olfaction. [3]

Astringency in coffee describes a tactile sensation rather than a taste, characterized by a dry, puckering feeling in the mouth similar to the experience of over-extracted espresso or strong black tea [1] . This sensation occurs when compounds in the brew bind with proteins in saliva, reducing lubrication and creating a rough, sometimes chalky mouthfeel [2] . While mild astringency can add complexity to a coffee’s sensory profile, excessive astringency is generally considered a defect in the cup.

Australia is a country and continent whose coffee identity is defined less by domestic production and more by a distinctive café culture built around espresso-based drinks. [1] In coffee terms, Australia matters as the primary cultural home of the flat white , a double-shot espresso with silky microfoam, and the long black , which is made by adding espresso to hot water rather than water to espresso. [1] The nation’s café scene, concentrated in urban centers like Melbourne and Sydney, is characterized by a strong preference for specialty roasts, skilled baristas, and a competitive café environment that has influenced coffee trends globally. [2] While Australia grows a small amount of coffee in Queensland and New South Wales, its global significance rests on consumption habits and café standards that have shaped how espresso drinks are prepared and ordered worldwide. [3]

Baggy Coffee refers to a traditional brewing method where coffee grounds are placed in a cup, then saturated with hot water and left to steep. After approximately 4 minutes, the grounds sink to the bottom [1] . The coffee becomes drinkable between 5-15 minutes after the initial break, allowing time for flavors to develop while the temperature drops to a comfortable drinking range [1] .

Baked Coffee A roasting defect characterized by flat, dull flavor profiles lacking complexity and vibrancy. Baked coffee results from insufficient heat application during the development phase after first crack [1] . The sensory profile has distinctly underwhelming characteristics: muted acidity , diminished sweetness, and a generic caramelized taste that lacks distinction [2] . When cupped, baked coffees often show a papery mouthfeel with minimal aromatic qualities.

Balance in coffee refers to a harmonious and pleasing equilibrium where no single attribute—acidity, sweetness, bitterness , body, or flavor—dominates over the others. This concept is one of the sought-after qualities in specialty coffee , distinguishing exceptional cups from good ones. A balanced coffee is not neutral; it can be complex and vibrant, but its elements are integrated and none are jarring or out of place.

Many coffee machines use pressure to enhance brewing parameters. Some of the devices that use pressure are single serve coffee machines , such as Keurig, or Tassimo, and espresso machines . Other devices are the Moka pot , or steam espresso makers. Pressure is measured in bar.

A barista (from the Italian for “bartender”) is a skilled professional, typically working in a café or coffeehouse, who specializes in preparing and serving espresso-based coffee drinks. In the specialty coffee industry, the role extends far beyond operating an espresso machine . A proficient barista is responsible for dialing in the espresso grind to achieve the proper extraction yield and balance, steaming milk to the correct texture and temperature for beverages like lattes and cappuccinos, and maintaining consistent quality and speed during service. This daily workflow is a practical application of brewing science, requiring an understanding of how variables like dose, yield, and time affect flavor .

Batian is a high-yielding, disease-resistant coffee variety developed by Kenya ’s Coffee Research Institute and released in 2010. This hybrid cultivar combines robust genetic resistance to both coffee leaf rust and coffee berry disease with a cup profile approaching the complexity of Kenya’s celebrated SL28 and SL34 varieties.

The main piece of a French press is a glass beaker. Because the beaker is exposed to high temperatures in a short time, they are subject to thermal shock , This is why beakers for French press coffee makers are made of borosilicate glass , or more recently, of stainless steel .

A bean hopper is the compartment atop a coffee grinder that stores whole coffee beans before grinding. Made from plastic, metal, or glass, it protects beans from light, air, and moisture—factors that harm freshness and flavor. [1] Its design controls bean flow into the grinder’s burrs, ensuring even grind size for consistent extraction . [2]

Beko is a domestic appliance and consumer electronics brand of Arçelik A. Ş.. Beko Elektronik A. Ş. (later Grundig Elektronik A. Ş. ) was a Turkish consumer electronics manufacturer, owned by Arçelik. In 2004 Beko Elektronik purchased Grundig and by January 2005, Beko and its rival Turkish electronics and white goods brand Vestel accounted for more than half of all TV sets manufactured in Europe. In April 2008 Beko renamed itself Grundig Elektronik A. Ş.

A Bialetti is an Italian brand synonymous with the Moka Express, a stovetop coffee maker invented by Alfonso Bialetti in 1933. [1] It has a distinctive octagonal aluminum body and brews espresso-like coffee by forcing steam-pressurized water through ground coffee. [2] Its affordability and simplicity democratized café-style brewing, establishing it as a global household staple. [3]

Invented in 1933 by Alfonso Bialetti, the Bialetti Moka Express is a stovetop coffee maker that uses steam pressure to make espresso-like coffee. [1] Its three-chamber design—a water-filled base, a middle funnel for ground coffee, and a top collector for the brew—relies on a pressure-driven mechanism. [2] When heated, steam pushes water through the grounds, creating a rich, concentrated coffee. [3]

Bica (pronounced BEE-kah) refers to Portugal ’s standard espresso -style coffee. It is a small, strong shot served in a demitasse cup and is known for being the default coffee ordered nationwide. [1] The term is often used interchangeably with um café (a coffee). As a type of espresso variation, it involves extracting a larger volume of water, which produces a smoother taste . [1] This characteristic flavor profile is linked to Portugal’s tradition of lighter coffee roasting .

Bicerin (pronounced bee-cheh-REEN) is a traditional layered coffee beverage from Turin, Italy. [1] Its name derives from the Piedmontese word for ‘small glass’. [2] The drink is a specific type of coffee-chocolate preparation, celebrated for its three distinct, un-stirred layers. [3]

Bisphenol A (BPA) is an organic compound with the chemical formula (CH3)2C(C6H4OH)2. It is a key building block for making clear, strong plastics and epoxy resins. First used commercially in 1957, its global production now reaches about 3.6 million tons every year. This BPA-based plastic is found in many everyday items, including water bottles, sports gear, and digital media like CDs. In industry, it has a crucial role in lining water pipes to prevent corrosion and coating the insides of many food and beverage cans, forming a protective barrier.

Bitterness represents one of the five basic tastes that the human palate can detect, with receptors concentrated primarily at the back of the tongue. In coffee, this fundamental taste sensation results from the extraction of specific compounds, particularly caffeine and certain phenolic acids. The primary chemical contributors to coffee’s bitter profile are caffeine and chlorogenic acid lactones, which develop during the roasting process . [1]
Black & Decker has a division of domestic coffee maker appliances. The division focuses on the auto drip coffee makers as the most popular coffee brewing method .

A Black Eye is a coffee drink composed of a standard drip coffee (typically 8-12 oz) with a double shot of espresso added to it [1] . The double shot of espresso contributes approximately 60mL of concentrated coffee, enhancing both the caffeine content and flavor profile [3] . While caffeine levels vary depending on factors such as bean type, roasting , and brewing methods , a Black Eye is likely to contain over 500 mg of caffeine per serving, significantly exceeding the daily recommended dose of 400 mg [3] . Compared to a Red Eye or Depth Charge, which includes a single shot of espresso and ranges from 250-400 mg of caffeine, the Black Eye offers a more potent caffeine boost [3] . Known for its robust and intense flavor, this drink strikes a balance between the strength of espresso and the milder taste of drip coffee [1] .

A blade grinder is a coffee grinding device that reduces roasted beans to particles using a rapidly spinning propeller-like blade mounted at the base of a small cup, rather than crushing them between two burr surfaces. [1] The distinction matters because grind uniformity governs extraction: blade grinders produce a wide spread of particle sizes, from fine dust to coarse chunks, so water extracts unevenly, yielding sour and bitter notes in the same cup. [2]

Blue Mountain Coffee is a legally protected Jamaican coffee appellation, not a coffee variety or brewing method, designating beans grown in a defined geographic zone within the Blue Mountains of eastern Jamaica. [1] The designation is restricted to coffee grown at elevations between 3,000 and 5,500 feet, a range that produces a slower-maturing cherry with a characteristically dense bean. [1]

Bodum, Inc. , (also known as BODUM) is a tableware and kitchenware company founded in Copenhagen, Denmark, in 1944 by Peter Bodum. In 1978, the son of the founder and new chief executive officer, Jørgen Bodum, moved the company to Switzerland to relocate Bodum to central Europe. Among the products Bodum makes are the Bodum French press , vacuum coffee brewers (the “Santos”), and double-walled beverage glasses made of borosilicate glass .

A boiler is a closed vessel in which water or other fluid is heated. The heated or vaporized fluid exits the boiler for use in various processes or heating applications, including boiler-based power generation, cooking, and sanitation.

Bolaven Plateau is a highland volcanic plateau in southern Laos, best known as the country’s primary coffee-growing region. [1] It is a distinct geographic origin rather than a coffee product or processing method, characterized by its cool, wet climate, basalt-rich soils, and elevations ranging from roughly 800 to 1,300 meters. [2] The plateau accounts for the vast majority of Laos’s commercial coffee production , with robusta dominating the output and arabica playing an increasingly important role in specialty markets. [3]

Bolivia is a coffee-origin term for arabica coffee grown in the South American country of Bolivia, where specialty production is concentrated in the high-elevation Yungas landscapes east of the Andes. [1] These are small-volume, high-altitude lots that often deliver a clean, sweet, and floral cup profile. Though a modest producer by global standards, Bolivia’s best coffees are increasingly valued by specialty buyers for their clarity and elegance — a reputation rooted in the country’s distinctive growing conditions. [2]

Bonavita is a coffee equipment brand established in 2009, known for affordable, precision-designed brewers and kettles catering to home and professional users. It gained prominence with SCA-certified automatic drip brewers, meeting strict specialty coffee standards for temperature and extraction . [1] The brand’s gooseneck kettles and pour-over brewers balance functionality, durability, and value, democratizing specialty coffee. [2]

Borosilicate glass is a type of glass with the main glass-forming constituents silica and boron oxide. Borosilicate glasses are known for having very low coefficients of thermal expansion (~3 × 10 /°C at 20°C), making them resistant to thermal shock, more so than any other common glass. Such glass is less subject to thermal stress and is commonly used for the construction of reagent bottles. Borosilicate glass is sold under such trade names as Kimax, Pyrex, Endural, Schott, or Refmex.

Bourbon refers to one of the two foundational varieties of Coffea arabica, alongside Typica, named for the island of Bourbon (now Réunion) where it was first widely cultivated. It is prized for a sweet, balanced, often fruit-forward cup and is the parent of many of today’s most important coffee varieties.

Brain damage , also called brain injury (BI), refers to damage to or the loss of brain cells. [1] These injuries can stem from a wide range of internal and external sources. In a coffee context, the term is used metaphorically to describe the catastrophic and irreversible overheating of coffee beans during roasting.

Brazil is the world’s largest coffee-producing country, supplying roughly a third of all coffee grown on earth. [1] Its output dwarfs every other origin, anchoring the global market and serving as the base of countless espresso blends thanks to its smooth, low-acid, chocolatey profile.

Bready coffee refers to under-roasted or underdeveloped coffee beans , characterized by flavors that suggest raw dough, bread, grains, or crackers. [1] This descriptor means a roast defect rather than an origin-specific characteristic; any coffee bean type can develop these qualities when subjected to improper roasting techniques. [2] The term emerged from modern specialty coffee roasting and quality control practices to diagnose and communicate roast profile flaws. [3]

The breve is a type of espresso-based beverage comparable to a caffè latte . The term refers to an American version that uses half-and-half instead of milk. This method produces a coffee drink known for its richer, creamier character than a traditional latte.

Breville refers to an Australian appliance manufacturer founded in 1932 by Bill O’Brien and Harry Norville in Sydney. The company name combines the founders’ surnames – “Bill” and “Norville” creating “Breville” [1] . Initially focused on radio components and mine detectors during World War II, Breville shifted to kitchen appliances in the post-war era. The brand gained prominence in the 1970s with the introduction of the sandwich toaster, which became synonymous with the Breville name in Australia and New Zealand.
Side view of a Slayer V3 boiler for a multi-group machine.

Brightness in coffee refers to a pleasant, tangy acidity that creates a lively and vibrant flavor experience. [1] This characteristic manifests as citrusy, fruity , or wine-like notes that add complexity and energy to each sip. [2]

The Brikka Pot, Bialetti’s stovetop espresso maker , distinguishes itself from traditional moka pots through its patented weighted valve, which produces a crema-like foam layer. [1] By dynamically regulating pressure (explained in Mechanism and Weighted Valve), the valve helps a richer, espresso-like extraction, improving texture and aroma. [2] This results in a velvety mouthfeel and intensified flavor, merging stovetop simplicity with espresso-machine quality. [3]

Briny describes a coffee taste that evokes the salty, savory character of seawater or brine, creating a brackish sensation on the palate. [1] This flavor descriptor is one of the most unwelcome characteristics a coffee can have, as it alters the expected taste profile in an unpleasant direction. [2]
Bucharest is a major coffee center, with one specialty café per 52,000 inhabitants, more than Berlin , or Copenhagen . The last years, the specialty coffee scene has grown exponentially.

Bunn-O-Matic Corporation is a manufacturer of coffee and tea-making equipment headquartered in Springfield, Illinois with a sister plant in Creston, Iowa. Founded by George Bunn, who invented the fluted coffee filter , its customers are primarily institutional foodservice providers. The company also offers a product line for home use and introduced the first commercial quality drip brewer for the home market in 1972. Its products are sold under the Bunn and Bunn-o-Matic brands.

A burr grinder is a coffee grinding device that uses two abrasive surfaces, called burrs, to crush coffee beans into particles of consistent size [1] . Unlike blade grinders that chop beans randomly, burr grinders control particle size by adjusting the distance between the two burrs [2] . This grinding mechanism has two primary variations: flat burr grinders, where parallel discs crush beans, and conical burr grinders, which use a cone-shaped burr inside a circular one [3] .

Burundi is a small, landlocked coffee-producing country in East Africa’s Great Lakes region and a rising specialty origin. Its high-grown, smallholder-produced Arabica coffees—almost exclusively Bourbon —are processed at centralized washing stations rather than on estates. [1] That model, combined with elevations that push toward 2,000 metres, has built a strong reputation for bright , sweet, berry-driven cups from hundreds of thousands of smallholder families. [2]

Cafecito (Spanish for “little coffee,” pronounced kah-feh-SEE-toh) is a small, intensely strong, and sweet coffee beverage that serves as the everyday name for Cuban-style espresso, also known as café cubano. [1] This variation of espresso stands apart through its preparation method and its central role in Cuban and Cuban-American social life. [1]

Cafestol is a diterpene molecule present in coffee. A typical bean of Coffea arabica contains about 0.6% cafestol by weight. Cafestol is present in its highest quantity in unfiltered coffee drinks such as French press coffee or Turkish coffee /Greek coffee. In filtered coffee drinks such as drip brewed coffee, it is present in only negligible amounts. Studies have shown that regular consumption of boiled coffee increases serum cholesterol by 8% in men and 10% in women. This increase in cholesterol, more specifically Low Density Lypoprotein (LDL) cholesterol has been linked to various cardiovascular diseases. Heavy consumption of cafestol is particularly a problem for those who have a genetic mutation that slows down metabolism of coffee in the body and is likely not an issue for the general population.

Caffè Americano, or Americano (English: American coffee) is a style of coffee prepared by adding hot water to espresso , giving it a similar strength to, but different flavor from regular drip coffee . The strength of an Americano varies with the number of shots of espresso and the amount of water added. The name is also spelled with varying capitalization and use of diacritics.

Caffeine is a bitter , white crystalline xanthine alkaloid that acts as a stimulant drug. Caffeine is found in varying quantities in the seeds, leaves, and fruit of some plants, where it acts as a natural pesticide that paralyzes and kills certain insects feeding on the plants, as well as enhancing the reward memory of pollinators.

Caffeine Extraction in Coffee Brewing Caffeine extraction occurs during the brewing process as water dissolves and pulls caffeine molecules from ground coffee. The extraction rate depends on several factors, including grind size , water temperature , and brewing time. Research shows that a standard brewing ratio of 15:1 (150g water to 10g coffee) provides optimal extraction conditions [1] . Grind size significantly impacts extraction – finer grinds increase surface area and caffeine extraction rates.

Caffè crema sometimes misspelled cafe crema, refers to two different espresso drinks. Caffè crema is an old name for espresso , and it was used in the 1940s and the 50s. The other drink named caffè crema is a long espresso drink originating in Europe. Caffè crema is primarily served in Switzerland, Austria and northern Italy, along the Italian/ Swiss and Italian/ Austrian border. Caffè crema generally means “espresso”. However, in technical discussions, referring to the long drink, it may be referred to as Swiss caffè crema.
Caffè Latte is a drink commonly prepared with one third espresso and two thirds steamed milk . The name is a portmanteau of the Italian words Caffè, which means coffee, and Latte, which means milk.

Caffè Mocha is a popular coffee beverage blending espresso, steamed milk , and chocolate, often finished with whipped cream. [1] [2] Its name originates from Mocha, Yemen, a historic port city renowned for its coffee trade and beans with a naturally chocolatey profile, which directly influenced the drink’s flavor concept. [1] It serves as a chocolate-infused version of a caffè latte or a hot chocolate enhanced with espresso. [1] [2]

Café au lait (French for “coffee with milk”) is a traditional coffee beverage consisting of equal parts brewed coffee and steamed milk [1] . Unlike a latte , which uses espresso and steamed milk with microfoam , café au lait typically has regular hot milk without the frothy texture. The drink is traditionally served in a wide-brimmed bowl or large cup, making it ideal for dipping pastries [2] .

Café Bombón (pronounced kah-FEY bohm-BON) is a traditional Spanish coffee drink and a popular variation of espresso . The drink consists of equal parts freshly brewed espresso and sweetened condensed milk. [1] It is known for its distinct two-layer appearance, which is presented in a small clear glass. [2] Originating from Spain ’s Valencia region, Café Bombón features a simple, sweet, and robust flavor profile. [3]

Café con Leche ( Spanish for “coffee with milk”) is a classic beverage of equal parts strong coffee, typically espresso , and scalded or steamed milk [1] . A staple in Spain and Latin America, it is traditionally served in a glass and is the regional equivalent of the French café au lait or Italian caffè latte [1] [2] .

Café Romano is a traditional Italian coffee preparation that combines espresso with lemon. It consists of a single or double shot of espresso served with either a slice of fresh lemon or lemon zest on the side. [1]

Camp Coffee is a concentrated liquid coffee essence that was a household staple in British kitchens throughout much of the 20th century. This dark, syrupy product combines coffee extract with chicory and sugar, creating a ready-to-use concentrate that requires only the addition of hot water or milk to make an instant coffee drink. The distinctive bottle design, featuring a Scottish Highland regiment soldier being served coffee by a Sikh soldier, became an iconic image on British grocery shelves.

Cancer (medical): a broad group of diseases characterized by unregulated cell growth and the formation of malignant neoplasms (tumors) that can invade nearby tissues and spread (metastasize) through the lymphatic system and bloodstream. On a coffee dictionary the entry covers what research says about coffee compounds and coffee drinking in relation to cancer risk.

A cappuccino, is an Italian coffee drink traditionally prepared with espresso, hot milk, and steamed-milk foam. Istituto Nazionale Espresso Italiano defines cappuccino as a beverage prepared with 25 ml espresso, and 100 ml steam-foamed milk. In coffee shops in North America, cappuccino is prepared with a doppio espresso and frothed milk up to 6 fl oz.

A cappuccino machine is an espresso machine equipped with a steam wand or built-in milk frother, designed to prepare espresso and steam milk for cappuccinos. These machines vary from manual models requiring skill to fully automatic ones that simplify milk frothing and espresso extraction . The steam wand, a critical component, uses pressurized steam to create microfoam, essential for the cappuccino’s creamy texture. [1] [2]
Capresso markets high-end coffeemakers, espresso machines, grinders, electric water kettles and frothers. The company is owned by Jura AG of Switzerland and was founded in 1994.

Caramelization refers to a form of non-enzymatic browning and a type of pyrolysis involving the thermal degradation of sugars, distinct from the Maillard reaction which requires amino acids. In coffee roasting , sucrose—the primary sugar in green coffee—breaks down through pyrolysis into simpler sugars and compounds. This process is known for generating sweet, nutty, buttery, and toffee-like flavors, while visually progressing the bean’s color from yellow through deepening browns.

Caramelly notes occupy the sweet segment of the coffee flavor wheel, positioned between chocolatey and vanilla subcategories. This descriptor refers to flavors reminiscent of caramelized sugar, butterscotch, and brown sugar in coffee. The perception of caramel sweetness is somewhat paradoxical, as research shows that roasting degrades 99 percent of sugars present in green coffee [1] . Despite this reduction, light-roasted coffees retain approximately 2.9 percent of the original sucrose content, while medium roasts preserve only 0.9 percent [2] .

Carbony is a flavor descriptor for coffee that evokes the aroma and taste of charcoal, burnt wood, or dark toast, typically associated with dark roasts [1] . This profile emerges as a foundational, bitter base note that defines many traditional espresso blends, French roasts, and Italian roasts [2] . The sensory experience centers on deep, smoky characteristics reminiscent of campfire embers or toasted bread crusts.

A Caro beverage is a caffeine-free coffee substitute made from roasted barley, malted barley, chicory, and rye, replicating coffee’s richness without the stimulant. [1] Originating in Germany, it is commonly prepared as an instant granular drink, offering a malty , slightly bitter flavor akin to coffee. [2] Ideal for those reducing caffeine , Caro preserves the ritual of a warm, robust beverage. [3]

Castillo is a modern, high-yielding Arabica coffee variety developed by Cenicafé , the research institute of Colombia ‘s National Federation of Coffee Growers, and released for commercial production in 2005. Bred specifically to withstand coffee leaf rust while preserving acceptable cup quality, it emerged from a cross between Caturra and the Timor Hybrid , introducing robusta genetics for resistance while selecting for Arabica-like flavor.

Catimor is not a single coffee cultivar but a family of related hybrid varieties derived from crossing Caturra with the Timor Hybrid , a natural arabica–robusta cross. [1] Breeders aimed to merge Caturra’s compact, productive plant form with strong genetic resistance to coffee leaf rust, one of the most devastating diseases affecting arabica coffee. [1]

Catuai (also spelled Catuaí) is a compact, high-yielding Arabica coffee cultivar developed in Brazil by crossing the Mundo Novo and Caturra varieties. [1] The Instituto Agronômico (IAC) in Campinas, São Paulo, created this hybrid to merge Caturra’s short stature with Mundo Novo ’s robust production, yielding a plant that is easy to harvest and highly productive per hectare. [1]

Caturra is a natural dwarf mutation of the Bourbon variety of Coffea arabica , first identified in Minas Gerais, Brazil , between 1915 and 1918. [1] A single-gene alteration shortens the tree’s internodes, producing a compact plant roughly two meters tall—about half the height of standard Bourbon—which simplifies hand-picking at harvest. [1]

Central Valley ( Costa Rica ) (Spanish: Valle Central) is a coffee-producing region in the heart of Costa Rica , specifically the highland basin surrounding the capital city of San José, including the provinces of Heredia and Alajuela. [1] This basin was the country’s original commercial coffee zone, where Arabica cultivation first took hold before spreading to other parts of the nation. [2]

Ceramic is an excellent material for the coffee industry. Its ability to conduct heat, which can be low or high depending on its specific makeup, makes it fit for a wide array of uses. The most common applications are coffee cups and mugs, where the right thermal traits keep a drink hot without making the outside too warm to hold. Ceramic kettles and pots are also popular, prized both for holding heat well and for their visual charm. Another important use is the coffee dripper, where ceramic aids in keeping a stable brewing temperature . Furthermore, ceramic coffee grinders mark a newer development; they are highly valued because the ceramic grinding burrs do not heat the coffee beans during the process, which protects the beans’ delicate flavors and aromas. This adaptability, coming from adjustable material properties, lets ceramics meet various functional and design needs throughout the entire coffee preparation and serving journey.

A cezve is a pot designed specifically to make Turkish coffee . The body and handle are traditionally made of brass or copper (occasionally silver or gold); though, recently, cezve are more commonly made from stainless steel , aluminium, or ceramics. The long handle is particularly useful to avoid burning one’s hands, and the brim is designed to serve the coffee. Other regional variations of the word cezve are jezve and čezve. In Ukrainian and Russian, the word is spelled джезва .

Chameleon Cold Brew is a brand of organic, ready-to-drink cold brew coffee concentrate known for its smooth, low-acid profile and versatility. Founded in Austin, Texas in 2010, it helped popularize high-quality cold brew by offering a convenient, shelf-stable concentrate that could be mixed with water or milk. [1] The brand uses beans from organic, fair-trade farms, focusing on ethical production and sustainability. [2] Its products include black coffee concentrate and flavored varieties, catering to different consumer tastes. [3]

Channeling (spelled Channelling in British English) refers to a critical defect in espresso brewing. This problem occurs when water under high pressure finds or creates uneven paths through the compressed coffee puck, bypassing much of the grounds. [1]
The Chemex Coffeemaker is a manual coffeemaker. It was introduced, and continues to be manufactured, by the Chemex Corporation in Pittsfield, Massachusetts. Peter Schlumbohm invented it in 1941.

Common chicory, Cichorium intybus, is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant usually with bright blue flowers, rarely white or pink. Various varieties are cultivated for salad leaves, chicons, or for roots (var. sativum), which are baked, ground, and used for preparing a beverage. It is also grown as a forage crop for livestock. It lives as a wild plant on roadsides in its native Europe, and in North America and Australia, where it has become naturalized.

China is a modern coffee origin shaped by rapid agricultural expansion and a domestic market that drinks a significant share of its own harvest. [1] Production is overwhelmingly concentrated in Yunnan province, which supplies over 98% of the national output, with smaller plantings in Fujian and Hainan. [1]

Chocolate Coffee Notes refers to a natural flavor and aroma profile in coffee that is characteristic of chocolate. This characteristic can range from sweet milk chocolate to dark chocolate or cocoa, and it develops through roasting chemistry without any added flavorings [5] . The profile is known for adding a comforting and rich dimension to coffee, and it is a feature of many popular coffee styles.

Cholesterol, a name that comes from the Greek words for bile (*chole-*) and solid (*stereos*), plus the chemical suffix *-ol*, is an organic molecule known as a sterol. It is a basic building block of animal cell membranes, where it has the key job of maintaining proper membrane permeability and structural fluidity. Beyond this cellular role, cholesterol serves as the necessary starting point for the body to make vital substances. These include steroid hormones, bile acids for digestion, and vitamin D.

Citrus in coffee refers to flavor notes that evoke fruits such as lemon, orange, grapefruit, or lime, characterized by bright acidity and a refreshing tang [1] . These flavors come from specific aromatic compounds present in coffee beans , which become detectable during tasting [2] . Citrus notes appear mostly in light to medium roast coffees, with African origins—particularly Ethiopia, Kenya, and Tanzania—often showing these characteristics [3] .

Clean coffee represents a category of high-quality, specialty coffee that prioritizes flavor clarity and artisanal production methods over mass-market approaches. This term refers to coffee produced through small-batch roasting, typically ranging from 5-25 kg per batch, which allows for precise control over the roasting process and enhanced flavor complexity.

A cocktail shaker in coffee context refers to the barware used to prepare chilled espresso -based beverages through shaking with ice. This technique produces drinks with a distinctive frothy, aerated texture that resembles cocktail preparation methods. [1] The shaking action creates a light, foamy consistency while rapidly chilling the espresso, resulting in a refreshing beverage with an enhanced mouthfeel compared to traditional iced coffee preparations. [2] Popular applications include the Italian Caffè Shakerato and modern specialty coffee interpretations. [3]

Coffea is a genus of flowering plants whose seeds, called coffee beans , are used to make coffee. It is a member of the Rubiaceae family. They are shrubs or small trees native to tropical and southern Africa and tropical Asia. Coffee ranks as one of the world’s most valuable and widely traded commodity crops and is an important export product of several countries. The plant is cultivated in over 70 countries, primarily in equatorial Latin America, Southeast Asia, India, and Africa.

Arabica ( Coffea arabica) Coffea arabica, commonly known as Arabica, is the world’s most widely cultivated coffee species, accounting for approximately 60-70% of global coffee production [1] . Native to the highlands of Ethiopia , this species grows best at elevations between 1,000-2,000 meters in subtropical climates with distinct rainy and dry seasons [2] . Arabica beans are distinguished by their oval shape and central crease, containing less caffeine (0.8-1.4%) than Robusta varieties [1] .

Coffea charrieriana (or Charrier coffee) is a species of flowering plant in the Rubiaceae family. It is a caffeine-free coffee found in Cameroon. This plant is the only known caffeine-free coffee plant from Central Africa. C. charrieriana was selected as one of “The Top 10 New Species” described in 2008 by The International Institute for Species Exploration at Arizona State University and an international committee of taxonomists.
Coffea liberica (or Liberian coffee) is a species of flowering plant in the Rubiaceae family. It is a coffee that is found in Liberia, West Africa.

The word “coffee” traces its roots to the Arabic “qahwah,” which originally referred to wine but later became associated with the beverage made from coffee beans [1] . This term evolved as it traveled through trade routes, becoming “kahve” in Turkish and eventually “coffee” in English by the 16th century.

Coffee Acidity is a fundamental sensory attribute in coffee tasting, referring to the bright, tangy, and vibrant sensation perceived on the palate, often characterized by fruity , citrus, or wine-like flavors. It is a key marker of quality and complexity , distinct from the scientific pH level of the beverage. The perceived acidity arises primarily from organic acids developed in the bean during growth, processing, and roasting .

Coffee Aroma Definition and Sensory Perception Coffee aroma refers to the complex mixture of volatile compounds that create the characteristic scent of coffee, detected primarily through the nose. The development of these aromatic compounds depends heavily on roasting temperature and duration. During roasting, green coffee seeds undergo significant chemical transformations as temperatures rise. When roasted at 180°C for varying durations, coffee develops distinct aromatic profiles based on roast level [1] .

A coffee bean refers to the dried and roasted seed of a tropical plant belonging to the genus * Coffea * [1] . Botanically, it is not a true bean but the pit found inside the coffee cherry fruit. The plural form is “coffee beans” [1] .

Coffee bloom refers to the rapid release of carbon dioxide gas that occurs when hot water first contacts freshly roasted coffee grounds. This process appears as a bubbling or swelling of the coffee grounds, often accompanied by a distinctive hissing sound. The mechanism behind blooming involves the displacement of trapped CO₂ gas that builds up during roasting . When water meets the grounds, this gas escapes rapidly, creating bubbles and temporarily preventing proper water saturation.

Coffee body, also called mouthfeel, refers to the perceived weight, thickness, and texture of coffee on the palate, ranging from thin and watery to full and syrupy. [1] This tactile sensation occurs independently from flavor, creating the physical impression of how coffee feels in the mouth rather than how it tastes. Body is primarily influenced by the concentration of soluble solids, oils, and fine particles suspended in the brewed coffee. [2]

Coffee Bouquet: The Aroma of Freshly Ground Coffee is the complete, complex scent released when whole coffee beans are ground [1] . It is a key sensory characteristic in professional coffee evaluation, consisting of hundreds of volatile aromatic compounds formed during roasting [4] . This fragrant preview is distinct from the aroma of the brewed coffee itself and plays a major role in shaping our overall perception of flavor [3] .
Coffee brewing refers to the preparation of the coffee beverage. There are many coffee brewing methods , and the extraction method can be different for these methods.

A coffee brewing method is a distinctive coffee preparation method, with specific brewing parameters, and using specific coffee making equipment. Some of the brewing parameters that can be altered to suit a coffee brewing method are:

Water temperature during coffee brewing determines the extraction yield, the total dissolved solids , and chemical profile of the coffee. All these parameters will affect the aroma and flavor of the final cup.

The Coffee Cabinet, despite its name, has no connection to coffee roasting or brewing. Instead, it means a regional beverage popular in Rhode Island and southeastern Massachusetts—a milkshake with coffee syrup and ice cream [1] . Rhode Islanders distinguish between “cabinets” and “milkshakes,” with the former containing ice cream and the latter being flavored milk.

Coffee concentrate is a highly concentrated coffee liquid crafted through a slow, cold extraction process—coarse coffee grounds steep in cold or room-temperature water for 12 to 24 hours before filtering. Unlike traditional hot brewing, this method yields a smooth, low-acidity concentrate valued for its versatility in both flavor and application. [1] [2]

Coffee culture describes a social atmosphere or series of associated social behaviors that depends heavily upon coffee , particularly as a social lubricant. The term also refers to the diffusion and adoption of coffee as a widely consumed stimulant by a culture. In the late 20th century, particularly in the Western world and urbanized centers around the globe, espresso has been an increasingly dominant form.
Explore the rich cultural traditions surrounding coffee. From cafe culture to coffee ceremonies, discover the social and cultural aspects of coffee around the world.

Extraction in the context of coffee brewing, is the process of dissolving soluble solids and emulsifying aromatic oils in water. Coffee extraction is a precise process, and there are a few parameters that will determine the taste, aroma, and strength of the brewed coffee. Correctly brewing coffee requires using the correct amount of coffee grounds, extracted to the correct degree, (largely determined by the correct time), at the correct temperature .

A coffee filter is a porous barrier, typically made of paper, cloth, or metal, used to separate coffee grounds from the brewed liquid during preparation. Its primary function is to clarify the final beverage by retaining solid particles.
Grind size is an important factor in coffee preparation, and it refers to the how fine or coarse the coffee bean is ground in order to prepare the coffee beverage.
A coffee grinder is a device for crushing coffee beans into fine grains or a powder. There are several types of coffee grinders, the most popular ones are burr grinders and blade grinders.

Coffee grinding is a critical step in the brewing process , enabling the extraction of soluble solids, caffeine , and oils from the coffee bean. [1] Without this process, extraction would be impossible even at high temperatures, as the compounds remain locked inside the whole bean. [2]
Aromatic oils are used in perfumery, cosmetics, flavoring of food, and in aromatherapy.

A coffee percolator is a type of pot used to brew coffee. The name stems from the word “percolate” which means to cause (a solvent) to pass through a permeable substance especially for extracting a soluble constituent. In the case of coffee-brewing the solvent is water, the permeable substance is the coffee grounds, and the soluble constituents are the chemical compounds that give coffee its color, taste, aroma, and stimulating properties.

Coffee production is the industrial process of converting the raw fruit of the coffee plant, known as a cherry, into the finished green coffee ready for roasting . This journey from farm to roaster is crucial, as each step directly shapes the flavor profile in your cup. The process begins with harvesting, followed by the critical stage of processing—removing the fruit pulp and mucilage from the seed. The method used here, whether washed, natural, or honey processed, has a profound impact on the resulting coffee’s acidity , body , and sweetness.

A coffee puck is the dense, disc-shaped cake of spent coffee grounds left in an espresso machine’s portafilter after extraction. This compacted mass—formed by tamping fresh grounds before brewing—serves as the foundation for balanced extraction, with its structure directly affecting water flow and extraction quality. [1] [2]

The Coffee Quality Institute (CQI) is a nonprofit organization founded in 1996, dedicated to enhancing coffee quality and improving the livelihoods of coffee farmers globally. [1] It is renowned for its Q Grader certification program, which standardizes cupping protocols to assess coffee quality consistently, fostering a universal language for evaluation. [2]

A coffee roasting company, or a coffee roaster for short, is a company that buys green coffee beans and roasts them. A coffee roaster sells various single origin or blends of coffee beans . There are various types of roasteries, depending on the niche and the company size. The third wave of coffee brought to the consumer’s attention micro roasters and artisan roasters, who cater to specialty coffee consumers and roast in small batches.

Roasting, in general, is a cooking method that uses dry heat, whether an open flame, oven, or other heat source. Roasting can enhance flavor through caramelization and Maillard browning on the surface of the food.

A coffee sock is a reusable cloth filter, typically made of cotton or linen, used to brew coffee by holding grounds as hot water passes through. Resembling a fabric pouch, often sock-shaped, it is suspended over a cup or pot via a wire frame or handle, a hallmark of Costa Rican chorreador or Southeast Asian kopi traditions. [1] [2]

A coffee substitute is a substance that is consumed instead of coffee . It will normally have coffee like properties such as taste and appearance. Coffee drinkers will often drink coffee substitutes if they are trying to avoid coffee but want to have the coffee experience.
Coffee tamping is the action of compacting ground coffee in an espresso portafilter with a tamp, prior to brewing .

The Coffee Triangle, also known as the Eje Cafetero, is the principal coffee-producing region in Colombia, encompassing the departments of Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda. [1] This is the geographic and cultural heart of Colombian coffee, where the Andes split into three ranges, creating steep slopes and fertile volcanic soils at altitudes between 1,300 and 1,900 meters. [2]
The coffee-to-water ratio—a fundamental metric in brewing—refers to the precise relationship between the mass of ground coffee and water, expressed as a weight-based proportion (e.g., 1:15). [1]

Coffeehouse, coffee shop, and café are related terms for an establishment which primarily serves prepared coffee or other hot beverages. It shares some of the same characteristics of a bar or restaurant, but it is different from a cafeteria. As the name suggests, coffeehouses focus on providing coffee and tea as well as light snacks.
Coffeemakers are devices or cooking appliances used to brew coffee . An appliance can also be referred to as a coffee machine.

Cold brew is a coffee preparation technique where coffee is extracted using cold water or at room temperature. Cold brew coffee is not the same as iced coffee , which refers to coffee that is brewed hot and then chilled by pouring over or adding ice.

A cold brew coffee maker is a specialized device designed for steeping coarsely ground coffee in cold or room-temperature water—typically for 12 to 24 hours—without heat. This slow extraction process yields a smooth, low-acid coffee concentrate, distinct from traditional hot-brewed methods. [1] Most models have a built-in filter or mesh system to separate grounds from the liquid after steeping, ensuring clarity. [2]

Colombia is one of the world’s leading coffee-producing countries and the most famous Arabica origin in the Americas. [1] Its washed, high-grown coffees set the global benchmark for balance, valued for a smooth, caramel-sweet cup with a bright, clean finish. [2]

Complexity in Coffee: A Symphony of Flavors is a metaphorical term describing the multi-layered, evolving flavor profile in coffee tasting [1] . Diverse sensory notes harmonize across aroma, taste, mouthfeel , and aftertaste like a musical symphony [1] . It is a characteristic of high-quality specialty coffee , focusing on the variety and transformation of distinct flavors [2] .

In coffee brewing, concentration is an important factor, determining the coffee strength, taste and flavor. In specialty coffee , Total Dissolved Solids concentration is an important factor. Many people are particularly interested in caffeine concentration.

Cortadito (from Spanish cortar , meaning “to cut”) refers to a Cuban espresso -based coffee drink . It is a sweetened cortado, where a shot of strong espresso is first mixed with sugar to create a creamy foam known as espumita . This mixture is then “cut” with a small amount of warm steamed or condensed milk. [1] [2]

A Cortado is a Spanish-origin coffee beverage consisting of one part espresso cut with an equal part of warm, lightly textured milk. [1] The name derives from the Spanish verb ‘cortar’ (to cut), referring to how the milk cuts the espresso’s acidity . [2] Originating in Spain’s Basque Country, it is a staple in Spanish and Portuguese cafés, defined by its small volume (4-6 oz) and balanced 1:1 to 1:2 espresso-to-milk ratio. [1] [3]

Costa Rica is a Central American coffee-producing country, and a country-level origin rather than a single farm, region, or processing method. Its export volume is modest, but its reputation for quality looms large, built on clean, bright, sweet arabica coffees. [1] That standing comes from a mix of legal protections and geographic advantages explored below, starting with the eight distinct growing regions that shape the national profile. [2]

Cowboy Coffee refers to a traditional coffee brewing method from the American West . This method involves adding coarsely ground coffee directly to a pot of boiling water over an open fire, which produces an unfiltered immersion brew. Cowboy coffee is known for its strong flavor and practicality. It plays a role in outdoor culture, as the process uses no specialized equipment beyond a pot and a heat source. [1]

Espresso crema is a brown, foamy layer on top of the brewed coffee. Crema is a mix of gas bubbles, and emulsified fats, which are the signature of a good espresso . The perfect crema is a reddish-brown foam, with tiny bubbles. If the bubbles are too big, the shot was incorrectly extracted. If the colour is too light is an under-extracted shot, and if it’s too dark, the shot is over-extracted.

Quality crema displays distinct visual and textural characteristics that distinguish exceptional espresso from mediocre shots. Premium crema is known for a rich golden-brown to reddish-brown color, forming a smooth, velvety layer that measures 3-5mm in thickness. This foam should persist for 2-3 minutes without dissipating quickly, maintaining complete surface coverage across the espresso shot. The texture plays a role in showing crucial quality indicators.

The crust in coffee cupping refers to the layer of coffee grounds that forms on the surface when hot water is poured over freshly ground coffee. This physical barrier develops as the grounds float and create a cohesive layer across the water’s surface.

Cuba is a Caribbean coffee origin defined by its small-scale production of Arabica beans grown in the island’s mountainous regions, particularly the Sierra Maestra and Escambray ranges. [1] In coffee terms, the name refers to the green coffee itself, not the sweetened espresso drinks that share the country’s name. [2]

Cuban espresso, known locally as ‘café cubano’ or ‘cafecito’, is a strong, sweetened shot of espresso that serves as a cornerstone of Cuban coffee culture [1] . It originated in Cuba during the early 20th century, evolving from Italian espresso traditions adapted to local tastes and the availability of cheaper, darker roasted beans.
Cuisinart is a brand for small kitchen appliances , especially the food processor of the same name, one of the first to become popular in the United States .

A coffee cup is a container thatcoffeeandespresso-based drinks are served in. Coffee cupsare made of porcelain, ceramic, or tempered glass and they can have a handlefor portability. Ceramic and porcelain provide insulation , maintaining the beverage hot. Tempered glassware needs a double wall construction in order to provide insulation.

A dallah is a traditional metal coffee pot , instantly recognizable by its distinctive long, curved spout. It is specifically designed for preparing Arabic coffee , holding a place of particular importance in Saudi coffee culture . The pot is not merely a tool for brewing but a central object in the social and ceremonial serving of coffee, reflecting deep-rooted customs of hospitality and community.

Dark roast refers to coffee beans roasted beyond the second crack, yielding a dark brown to nearly black appearance with an oily sheen—a visual hallmark of this intense roast level. [1] The extended roasting process develops a bold, smoky flavor profile marked by pronounced bitterness and low acidity, characteristics rooted in traditional French and Italian roasting traditions. [2]

Decaffeination refers to extracting at least 97% of caffeine from green coffee beans before roasting [1] . The process began commercially in 1905 when Ludwig Roselius developed a benzene-based method [2] . Today, four main techniques are used: Direct Solvent, Indirect Solvent, Swiss Water, and Carbon Dioxide.

A decanter is a vessel that is used to hold the decantation of a liquid which may contain sediment. Decanters are normally used as serving vessels for wine. Decanters vary in shape and design. They are usually made of an inert material and will hold at least one standard bottle of wine (0.75 litre). A similar kind of vessel, the carafe /kəˈræf/, is used for serving wine as well as other drinks, but is not supplied with a stopper.

Degassing refers to the natural process where freshly roasted coffee beans release trapped gases, primarily carbon dioxide (CO₂). This release occurs after roasting and plays a crucial role in achieving balanced flavor during brewing. The required resting period can range from a few hours to several days, depending on roast level and brewing method. This process is a standard practice in specialty coffee worldwide.

Dementia (from Latin dementia , ‘madness’) refers to a medical condition characterized by a serious, progressive decline in global cognitive ability, including thinking, reasoning, memory, and emotional regulation, often resulting from widespread brain injury or neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer’s. This static, global impairment manifests as a loss of vibrancy and richness in mental function, akin to the flat, lifeless sensory experience of underdeveloped coffee beans known for a baked flavor profile.

A demitasse is a small cup used to serve Turkish coffee or espresso . In some languages it is called fincan, fildžan, filxhan or φλιτζάνι (flidzáni). In Spanish, it is called a pocillo. It typically has about 60–90 ml capacity — half the size of a full coffee cup (a tasse à café is about 120 ml). Typically they are made of white pottery or porcelain and accompanied by matching saucers, but some coffeehouses and companies from chinaalso produce brightly decorated varieties.

Descaling removes mineral buildup—primarily calcium and limescale—from coffee equipment after repeated heated water exposure. These deposits accumulate in critical components like boilers, pipes, and group heads, impairing heat transfer and restricting water flow while introducing off-flavors by disrupting extraction. [1]

De’Longhi Group, or De’Longhi S.p. A, is a major Italian small appliance manufacturer based in Treviso, Italy. They manufacture coffee making equipment, including drip coffee makers and espresso machines.

Diabetes mellitus, commonly called diabetes, is a chronic metabolic disorder marked by persistently elevated blood glucose levels from defects in insulin secretion, insulin action, or both. [1] The two principal forms are type 1, an autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic beta cells, and type 2, a progressive insulin resistance paired with relative insulin deficiency. [1]

Dialing In (spelled dialling in in UK/ Australia ) refers to the process of adjusting an espresso machine and grinder to produce a balanced shot from a specific coffee. This daily routine involves fine-tuning several variables based on taste . The term comes from the act of turning a grinder’s dial to change the fineness of the coffee grounds, a setting that plays a crucial role in extraction. [1]

Dissolution is the process by which a solute forms a solution in a solvent. The solute, in the case of solids, has its crystalline structure disintegrated as separate ions, atoms, and molecules form. For liquids and gases, the molecules must be adaptable with those of the solvent for a solution to form. The outcome of the process of dissolution (the amount dissolved at equilibrium.

Doi Chang (ดอยช้าง, also transliterated as Doi Chaang) is a mountain and coffee-producing village area in Mae Suai District, Chiang Rai Province, northern Thailand, best known for producing single-origin Arabica coffee under the Doi Chaang/Doi Chang name. [1] It is a specific geographic origin and village-based producer identity, not a generic Thai coffee term or a national brand.

Doi Tung is a single-origin Arabica coffee and a Geographical Indication (GI)-protected product from the Doi Tung Development Project area in Chiang Rai province, northern Thailand, near the borders with Myanmar and Laos. [1] Grown under forest shade on highland slopes, its identity comes from mountain origin and a royal development program. [2]
The Nescafé Dolce Gusto is an espresso machine /coffee capsule system from Nestlé. The machines are produced by hardware manufacturers Krups and De’Longhi .

Dominican Republic is a Caribbean coffee-producing country and coffee origin located on the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti. [1] It is known primarily for its Arabica coffees grown in mountainous regions, with most production centered in the highlands of Barahona, Cibao, Juncalito, and Ocoa. [2]
Dorian Bodnariuc is the founder of Coffee-Brewing-Methods.com . He started his coffee career as a barista, then moved in the IT, but he kept the contact with the coffee industry.
Coffee brewing requires following strict recipes. This includes brewing temperature , coffee grind size , brewing time and the coffee dose.

Double, in the context of espresso brewing , refers to the volume of coffee pulled at one time. A double shot of espresso is pulled from approximately 14 grams of coffee grounds. The filter basket used for pulling it, is also called a double, and it can hold 14 grams of coffee grounds. The double espresso shot is also called a doppio, the Italian word for double.

Double Fermentation (also called double washed or double soaking in Kenya) is a coffee processing variation in which the mucilage—the sticky fruit layer surrounding the coffee bean—is broken down in two separate fermentation stages rather than one. [1] It modifies the standard washed process by adding a post-wash fermentation or soak in clean water. [2]

DR Congo (also known as the Democratic Republic of the Congo) is a large coffee-producing origin in Central Africa, distinct from its smaller neighbor, the Republic of the Congo. [1] It is best known for high-grown, washed Arabica coffee, particularly Bourbon-related varieties cultivated in the eastern highlands. [2]

A drink, or beverage, is a kind of liquid which is specifically prepared for human consumption. There are many groups of drinks. It can be divided into various groups such as plain water, alcohol, non alcoholic drinks, soft drinks (carbonated drinks), fruit or vegetable juices and hot drinks. In addition to fulfilling a basic need, drinks form part of the culture of human society.

Drip Coffee, or filtered coffee, is a method which involves pouring water over roasted, ground coffee beans contained in a filter, creating the beverage called coffee. Water seeps through the ground coffee, absorbing its oils and essences, solely under gravity, then passes through the bottom of the filter. The used coffee grounds are retained in the filter with the liquid falling (dripping) into a collecting vessel such as a carafe or pot.

A drip tray is a removable grate and reservoir positioned beneath an espresso machine’s group head, serving as the first line of defense against spills by collecting excess water, stray coffee grounds, and beverage overflow during brewing. This component does more than contain mess—it prevents liquid and residue buildup that could compromise machine surfaces or countertop hygiene. [1]

A dual boiler espresso machine features two dedicated boilers—one for brewing and another for steaming—enabling independent temperature control for simultaneous operation. Unlike single-boiler models, this design eliminates task-switching delays, ensuring precise extraction temperatures and stable steam pressure . The brew boiler optimizes flavor extraction, while the steam boiler delivers consistent microfoam for milk drinks. [1] [2] [3]

Dunkin’ Donuts is an American global doughnut company and coffeehouse chain based in Canton, Massachusetts. It was founded in 1950 by William Rosenberg in Quincy, Massachusetts. Its logo is two D’s side by side in orange and hot pink. The company primarily competes with Starbucks , as over half the company’s business is in coffee sales, and with Krispy Kreme for doughnut sales.

E-61 is a class of espresso machine , defining a standard size and fitting for the portafilter which holds the ground coffee. E-61 is a common standard for commercial espresso machines. The name E-61 comes from the Faema E-61 espresso machine, which was named for the solar eclipse in its year of introduction, 1961.

Earthy coffee presents a distinctive sensory experience characterized by rich, natural flavors that evoke soil, wood, and herbs . This flavor profile creates a connection to the earth through its deep, grounding taste sensations that coffee enthusiasts describe as reminiscent of forest floors or freshly turned garden soil. The aroma of earthy coffee typically carries notes of damp earth, mushrooms, and sometimes cedar or other woody elements .

Ecuador is a coffee-producing country on South America’s Pacific coast, known for its remarkable geographic diversity that yields both commercial-grade lowland coffee and high-grown specialty Arabica. Cultivation spans four distinct zones—coastal lowlands, Andean highlands, the Amazon, and the Galápagos Islands—making it one of the most ecologically varied origins in the world. The southern Andean provinces deliver its most celebrated coffees, where high elevations and cool climates produce sweet, floral, and complex cups that have earned increasing attention from specialty roasters. [1]

El Salvador is a coffee origin from the small Central American nation of the same name, known for highland, volcanic-grown Arabica coffees with a clean, sweet cup profile. [1] Its growing heritage dates to 1740, when coffee first arrived from the Caribbean islands, and the crop soon became the backbone of the national economy—at one point ranking the country among the world’s top five producers. [2]

An Easy Serving Espresso Pod, or E.S.E. pod, is a small coffee disc (Coffee pod), packed in a paper filter covering. Each pod contains 7 grams of compressed ground coffee, ready to be extracted into a shot. A double serving pod, (doppio), contains 14 grams of ground coffee. Pods are typically 44-45mm size for E.S.E. certified machines. There are many Espresso machines that can use the 45 mm diameter E.S.E Espresso standard Pod.

Espressino (pronounced es-press-EE-no, from the Italian diminutive suffix ‘-ino’ meaning ‘small’) is a small Italian coffee beverage that is a regional variation of a cortado or macchiato with chocolate. It originates from the Puglia (Apulia) region in southern Italy. [1] The drink is defined by its combination of a single shot of espresso , a small amount of frothed milk, and cocoa powder or chocolate spread. [2]
Espresso is a rich, concentrated coffee drink. The standard serving, a shot, is brewed by forcing pressurized hot water through finely ground coffee beans .

Espresso beans are coffee beans roasted and blended specifically for espresso preparation, typically with a darker roast profile. While any bean can be used for espresso, those labeled as ‘espresso beans’ are optimized for high-pressure extraction , yielding a balanced, concentrated shot with lower acidity and richer body. These qualities make them ideal for milk-based drinks like lattes and cappuccinos. [1] [2]

An espresso blend combines beans from multiple origins, roasted and blended to create a balanced, flavorful shot when extracted under high pressure. Crafted to highlight complementary flavors, these blends emphasize sweetness, body , and acidity while ensuring batch-to-batch consistency. [1] A well-designed blend has equal appeal in straight espresso and milk-based drinks, delivering harmony whether enjoyed alone or with dairy. [2]

Espresso con panna, Italian for “espresso with cream,” refers to a standard shot of espresso topped with a dollop of whipped cream [1] . The whipped cream gradually melts into the espresso, creating a sweetened and textured drinking experience without additional sugar. This preparation highlights the intensity of espresso while softening its edge with the richness of cream. Some variations include a light dusting of cocoa powder or a drizzle of caramel as optional garnishes [2] .
The espresso macchiato is a coffee espresso drink with a small amount of steamed milk , usually as foam, on top.

An espresso machine is used to produce the traditional Italian coffee beverage called espresso . The espresso maker brews coffee by forcing hot water through a puck of compacted ground coffee. The result is a concentrated coffee, with a thick consistency, called espresso.

The Espro P7 features a double-walled stainless steel French press design with a patented two-stage micro-filter system, minimizing sediment while preserving coffee’s natural oils and full-bodied texture. [1] Developed by Canadian brand Espro, it combines immersion brewing benefits with a cleaner cup, eliminating paper filters entirely. [2] Its dual precision filters (fine and ultra-fine mesh) trap grounds without over-extraction, ensuring a balanced, grit-free brew. [3]

Espuma (also known as espumita in some Cuban-American communities) is the sweet, whipped foam that crowns Cuban-style espresso drinks such as the cafecito and colada. This pale, caramel-colored emulsion forms when the first concentrated drops of freshly brewed espresso are beaten with sugar into a thick, aerated paste. [1]

Ethiopia, officially the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, is a country in the Horn of Africa. It shares borders with Eritrea to the north, Djibouti and Somalia to the east, Sudan and South Sudan to the west, and Kenya to the south. With a population of over 91 million, it is the most populous landlocked country in the world and the second-most populous nation on the African continent.

Extraction time—the period from water’s initial contact with coffee grounds to the final drip—determines flavor balance by regulating the dissolution of soluble compounds: acids, sugars, and bitter elements. Shorter extractions (e.g., espresso) highlight bright acidity but may lack sweetness, yielding a sour taste. Longer extractions (e.g., immersion brewing ) risk over-extracting tannins, introducing astringency. [1] [2] [3]

Extraction yield measures the percentage of coffee solids dissolved into the brewed liquid, calculated as extracted solubles relative to the original dry coffee mass. This metric shapes flavor balance by determining how much of the coffee’s key compounds (acids, sugars, and bitter elements) transfer during brewing. In specialty coffee , the 18–22% range is widely targeted for optimal extraction, where sweetness, acidity , and bitterness harmonize. [1] [2]

Ferment flavor in coffee refers to the distinctive sensory characteristics in the cup that develop when coffee cherries undergo controlled microbial activity during post-harvest processing. This flavor profile, valued by baristas and roasters , typically presents as bright acidity with fruity , winey , or complex notes.

Filter Basket: Definition and Core Function A filter basket is a perforated metal component that fits inside an espresso machine ‘s portafilter, designed to hold ground coffee during the brewing process . It has tiny holes through which pressurized hot water passes, extracting flavor compounds from the coffee grounds. Filter baskets come in various sizes, with 18g capacity being recommended for consistent home brewing [1] . While 8g baskets exist for single shots, they present extraction challenges [2] .

Filtration is commonly the mechanical or physical operation which is used for the separation of solids from fluids (liquids or gases) by interposing a medium through which only the fluid can pass. Oversize solids in the fluid are retained, but the separation is not complete; solids will be contaminated with some fluid and filtrate will contain fine particles (depending on the pore size and filter thickness).

A Filtron is a gravity-fed cold brew coffee maker designed for slow, controlled extraction—typically one drop per second—over 12-24 hours. Modeled after Japanese Kyoto-style brewers, its three-part system (water reservoir, filter chamber, and carafe) ensures even saturation while minimizing agitation. [1] [2]

The Flat White is a distinct coffee preparation that emerged from Australia and New Zealand before gaining international popularity. Traditionally served in a 180 ml ceramic cup in Australia, the Flat White contains less milk than the Australian latte, which typically comes in a 200 ml glass [1] . This smaller milk-to-coffee ratio creates a more concentrated flavor profile. Size specifications vary globally, with the authentic Flat White measuring approximately 162 ml (5.5 oz) [2] .

A flat white is a coffee beverage consisting of espresso topped with microfoam-textured milk [1] . Distinguished by its velvety texture and strong coffee flavor, it is typically served in a small cup (5-8oz/150-240ml) to maintain a coffee-forward profile [1] .

Flavor or flavour is the sensory impression of a foods, drinks, or other substances, and is determined mainly by the chemical senses of taste and smell. The “trigeminal senses”, which detect chemical irritants in the mouth and throat as well as temperature and texture, are also very important to the overall Gestalt of flavor perception. The flavor of the food, as such, can be altered with natural or artificial flavorants, which affect these senses.
