Flavored coffee refers to coffee beans treated with natural or artificial flavoring agents—typically after roasting—to create distinct aromatic and taste profiles. These oil-based flavorings, ranging from vanilla to seasonal spices, originated to enhance lower-quality beans but now cater to consumers seeking consistent, dessert-like experiences without extra additives. [1] [2]

Floral notes in coffee represent aromatic and flavor characteristics that evoke flowers, ranging from delicate jasmine and rose to bright lavender and orange blossom. These sensory qualities emerge from complex interactions between coffee origin, post-harvest processing methods, roasting techniques, and brewing parameters. Processing methods influence floral expression.

Flow rate quantifies the speed of water moving through coffee grounds during brewing, measured in grams per second. In espresso, this metric tracks water exiting the portafilter; for pour-overs, it governs drainage through the filter. This critical variable shapes extraction, influencing contact time and extraction outcomes. [1]
Foam is an important aspect of coffee preparation, and it determines, or validates quality in some coffee drinks.

Food is any substance consumed to provide nutritional support for the body . It is usually of plant or animal origin, and contains essential nutrients, such as carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, or minerals. The substance is ingested by an organism and assimilated by the organism’s cells in an effort to produce energy, maintain life, or stimulate growth. Historically, people secured food through two methods: hunting and gathering, and agriculture.

FrancisFrancis! is an espresso machine manufacturer owned by illy. Founded in 1994 by Francesco Illy , FrancisFrancis produces espresso machines for the home market. Italian architect Luca Trazzi was responsible for the aesthetics. In 2004 the company was purchased by illy. Since then, FrancisFrancis! have become the espresso machines of choice for illy; always associated with the coffee brand. Various FrancisFrancis! machines are designed by other award-winning designers and are considered a piece of industrial art on their own. The Francis Francis! espresso makers were some of the first to feature the option of E.S.E. pods. Later on, illy introduced the iperEspresso system which produces one of the best capsule based espresso beverages.

Frappuccino is a trademarked line of blended coffee beverages sold by Starbucks . It consists of coffee , blended with ice and other various ingredients, usually topped with whipped cream. Frappuccinos are also sold as bottled coffee beverages in stores and from vending machines.

The Frappé is a shaken or blended iced coffee beverage famously reliant on instant coffee as its base. This choice highlights the tension between accessibility and specialty values. Nearly 50 percent of the world’s coffee crop is processed into instant coffee. [1] For coffee professionals, the Frappé is known for its unique preparation method, where agitation creates a stable, creamy foam without dairy. This technique plays a role in understanding emulsion and texture in other coffee applications, from whipped coffee to shaken espresso .

French drip is a manual coffee brewing method that uses a special carafe. The carafe has a filter and a lid that are placed on top. The brewing technique is similar to other manual drip coffee brewing methods . Coffee is coarsely ground and placed in the filter. The filter is placed on top of the carafe, and it is designed to fit snugly. Then hot water is poured over the coffee grounds. The filter retains the grounds, while brewed coffee passes through in the pot. At the end the filter is covered with a lid that prevents coffee from getting cold.

The French press is a simple coffee maker , consisting of a brewing recipient and a filter-plunger. The brewing recipient can be made of glass, or stainless steel , or ceramic . The plunger has a screen filter attached at the bottom and is used to separate the coffee grounds from the brew. The screen is made from stainless steel, or sometimes from plastic.

Fruity notes in coffee refer to the aromatic and flavor characteristics reminiscent of various fruits detected during a coffee cupping or brew evaluation [1] . These notes are categorized into distinct sensory groups central to coffee flavor profiling. Berry notes include raspberry and blueberry characteristics prized in some African coffees, while citrus covers lemon and orange impressions. Stone fruit notes show peach and plum qualities, and tropical fruit notes include pineapple and passion fruit [2] .

Full immersion is a coffee brewing method where ground coffee remains fully submerged in water throughout extraction, ensuring even saturation and uniform flavor development. Unlike percolation methods—which pass water through grounds once—full immersion maintains continuous contact, yielding a balanced, full-bodied cup. This approach prioritizes control, enabling precise adjustment of steep time, temperature, and agitation to influence extraction. [1] [2]

Gaggia is an Italian company that makes coffee machines, especially espresso and cappuccino machines, in addition to small kitchen appliances . The company is mainly owned by Saeco International Group, a division of Dutch consumer electronics giant Philips.

The Gaggia Classic Pro is an entry-level semi-automatic espresso machine crafted by Italian manufacturer Gaggia for home use. Designed with commercial-grade components like a 58mm portafilter and a three-way solenoid valve, it bridges professional and domestic espresso-making. [1] Its robust construction and straightforward design make it ideal for mastering techniques such as shot extraction and milk texturing. [2]

Galão ( Portuguese pronunciation: [ɡɐˈlɐ̃w̃]) refers to a traditional Portuguese hot coffee drink . It consists of one part espresso combined with three parts foamed milk, served in a tall glass. [1] This beverage is a type of Portugal’s standard café-style latte and is known for its mild, creamy flavor profile. [2] The name translates to “gallon,” which means the drink’s substantial milk volume. [3]

Geisha (also spelled Gesha) is a distinct variety of Arabica coffee originally collected from Ethiopia’s rainforests and later popularized through Panama , where it produces some of the world’s most celebrated and expensive cups. Its intensely floral, tea-like character sets it apart from nearly all other coffee varieties.

A God shot can be described as a perfect shot achieved from an espresso machine , where the recipe and all of the parameters that go into espresso brewing such as bean type, roast, grind size , dose, water volume and temperature , as well as properly maintained and clean machinery all align to produce a coffee shot that is considered to be perfect by the taster, barista or customer.

Grassy notes in coffee represent a distinct flavor characteristic that manifests as fresh-cut grass, hay, or herbaceous qualities in the cup. [1] These flavors typically indicate underdeveloped coffee beans or processing issues that prevent proper flavor maturation during roasting. [2] The identification and classification of such defects is known for increasing sophistication through research initiatives.

The grouphead is the component of an espresso machine where the portafilter attaches, housing the dispersion screen and gasket that distribute hot water evenly to the coffee puck. It functions as the critical interface between the machine and the coffee, enabling precise water distribution and temperature control during extraction. [1] [2]

Guatemala is a coffee origin, not a coffee variety or brewing method: it refers to coffees grown in Guatemala, typically high-grown Arabica known for a chocolatey, often spicy cup with bright acidity and strong regional character. [1] It is distinct because Guatemalan coffee is marketed by named producing regions whose climates and volcanic soils shape flavor differences. [2] The country is one of Central America’s most celebrated coffee producers, with a crop that is almost entirely washed and grown at elevations from 1,300 to 2,000 metres. [3]

Hamilton Beach Brands, Inc. is an American manufacturer of home appliances , air purifiers, and commercial restaurant equipment marketed primarily in the United States, Canada , and Mexico including: Blenders, Mixers, Toasters, Slow cookers, Irons and Air purifiers. Until sometime in the 1980s the company’s products were marketed under the brand name “Hamilton Beach Scovill”, reflecting a merger that occurred in the 1940s.

Handpresso SARL is a French manufacturer of portable espresso machines . Founded in Fontainebleau in 2006 by Henrik Nielsen as a spin-off from Nielsen Innovation SARL. Handpresso is inspired by Danish Design and has created and patented the world’s first handheld espresso coffeemaker, Handpresso WILD ESE, which is sold in 25 countries. The first Handpresso machines were designed for E.S.E. coffee pods . In the year 2008, Handpresso won 7 international design prizes including IF and Formland.

Hario is a Japanese company specializing in high-quality glassware and coffee brewing equipment, renowned for its V60 pour-over dripper. Founded in 1921 as a manufacturer of laboratory glass, Hario transitioned to coffee products, leveraging its expertise in heat-resistant materials to create precise, durable tools. [1] The V60, introduced in the 2000s, features a distinctive cone shape with spiral ribs, promoting even extraction. [2]

The Hario V60 is a cone-shaped pour-over coffee dripper designed by the Japanese company Hario. Its distinctive V-shaped 60-degree angle and spiral ribs are core elements driving its brewing mechanics. This design combines a large single hole with a ridged interior to create a dynamic flow path, enabling precise control over water dispersion and extraction. [1] [2]

Harsh coffee represents an undesirable flavor profile characterized by sharp, aggressive, and unpleasant sensory experiences. This negative descriptor includes off-putting characteristics that make coffee difficult to enjoy, typically featuring bitter compounds that create an astringent, mouth-puckering sensation. These flavors often present as metallic, acrid, or burning notes that linger.

The heart is a hollow muscle that pumps blood throughout the blood vessels by repeated, rhythmic contractions . It is found in all animals with a circulatory system. The term cardiac means “related to the heart” and comes from the Greek καρδιά, kardia, for “heart”.

A heat exchanger is a piece of equipment built for efficient heat transfer from one medium to another. The media may be separated by a solid wall, so that they never mix, or they may be in direct contact. They are widely used in space heating, refrigeration, air conditioning, power plants, chemical plants, petrochemical plants, petroleum refineries, natural gas processing, and sewage treatment.

Definition and Lexicon Placement “Herbal” serves as a primary descriptor in coffee tasting vocabulary, identifying flavor notes that resemble fresh or dried herbs such as sage, thyme, basil, or oregano. This term occupies a distinct position within established coffee flavor lexicons, including the Specialty Coffee Association’s Flavor Wheel, where it falls under the broader category of plant-like qualities [1] .

A hermetic seal has the quality of being airtight. In common usage, the term often implies being impervious to air or gas. When used technically, it is stated in conjunction with a specific test method and conditions of usage.

Hidey is a coffee tasting term describing a specific, often undesirable, flavor note in a brew, reminiscent of animal hides or leather [1] . This descriptor emerged in professional cupping to identify a pungent savory note that differs from standard earthy defects in a roast [2] . It captures an animalistic quality that separates it from other off-flavors in the coffee lexicon.

High-density lipoprotein (HDL) is one of the five main types of lipoproteins that carry fats like cholesterol and triglycerides through the watery environment of the blood. These particles are often listed by size, from the largest to the smallest: chylomicrons, very- low-density lipoprotein (VLDL), intermediate-density lipoprotein (IDL), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) , and finally HDL. In a person with good health, roughly thirty percent of the total blood cholesterol is transported by HDL particles. Standard blood tests measure HDL-C, which refers specifically to the amount of cholesterol found inside these HDL carriers.

Home appliances are electrical/mechanical machines which accomplish some household functions, such as cooking or cleaning. Home appliances can be classified into: Major appliances, or White goods, Small appliances, or Brown goods Consumer electronics, or Shiny goods. The consumer electronics division is also notable for the maintenance and repair of these kinds of products.

Honduras is a coffee origin, not a specific variety or brewing method, referring to green coffee produced in the Central American nation of Honduras, the largest coffee-producing country in the region by volume. [1] High-grown Arabica coffees from six distinct growing regions define it, each contributing a unique cup profile. [2]

Honey Process (also known as miel in Spanish-speaking regions) is a post-harvest coffee processing method in which the outer skin of the coffee cherry is mechanically removed, but some or all of the sticky mucilage is left on the parchment layer during drying. [1]

Hot chocolate, traditionally made from melted chocolate or cocoa powder mixed with milk or water, is sweetened and enhanced with vanilla or spices. As a caffeine-free option, it holds a significant place in coffee culture, historically served in European coffeehouses alongside espresso drinks. [1] Today, specialty cafés treat it with the same care as coffee, using high-quality cocoa and refined techniques. [2]

A hot plate is a small, portable tabletop appliance that has one or more electric heating elements or gas burners. This self-contained unit works on its own but often acts as a substitute for a single burner from a full-sized stove . Its compact and standalone design makes it a highly versatile tool for locations without a full kitchen, including dormitory rooms, office break areas, small apartments, and outdoor spaces. The device offers a direct and adjustable source of heat for various cooking jobs such as boiling water, simmering sauces, or frying foods. Its simplicity and portability have secured its place in both domestic and professional settings where a permanent cooking installation is impractical or unavailable.

Hypertension (HTN or arterial hypertension) is a chronic condition of elevated arterial blood pressure , summarized by systolic pressure—the higher number measuring arterial pressure during heartbeats when the heart muscle contracts—and diastolic pressure—the lower number measuring pressure between beats when the heart is relaxed. This elevation requires the heart to work harder than normal.

Iced coffee is a cold variant of coffee. In more recent times it has become common for coffee shops to offer ‘iced’ versions of their most popular coffee drinks. The iced latte and iced mocha are the two most common examples of this. A quick way of preparing such drinks is to make a small quantity of strong, hot espresso , dissolving the required sweetener/flavorings in the hot liquid and then pouring this directly into a cup of ice cold milk. This method is common in busier coffee shops. The hot coffee can also be cooled using cold water, ice, cream or ice cream.
An iced latte typically refers to a beverage that is prepared with freshly brewed, hot espresso and chilled milk over ice. This drink is very typical in the United States.
The iced mocha is a variant of the iced latte and another beverage that would fall into the bracket of iced coffee .

illycaffè is a brand of coffee produced in Trieste, Italy. illy produces principally one blend in three roast variations: normal, dark roast , and decaffeinated. The blend is packaged as whole beans, pre-ground coffee, E.S.E. pods , or iperEspresso Capsules.

Immersion brewing extracts coffee by fully submerging grounds in water for a controlled time before separation. Unlike percolation—where water flows through grounds once—immersion ensures uniform saturation through prolonged contact, producing balanced extraction. This principle underpins devices like the French press, inverted AeroPress, and cupping protocols. [1] [2] [3]

Immersion cold brew is a coffee preparation method where coarsely ground coffee steeps in cold or room-temperature water for 12 to 24 hours before filtration. Unlike drip or flash-chilled methods, immersion brewing achieves full saturation of grounds, allowing a slow, balanced extraction that boosts sweetness while cutting acidity. [1] [2]

India is a major coffee-producing country in South Asia, with its traditional coffee belt concentrated in the southern states of Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu. [1] As a coffee term, it refers to the geographic origin and production context of Indian coffee rather than a specific processing style or cultivar.

Indian Filter Coffee refers to a distinctive coffee beverage characterized by its thick, syrupy consistency and robust flavor profile. The drink is prepared using a traditional two-chamber metal filter device specific to South Indian coffee culture . The coffee consists of pre-ground arabica and/or robusta beans blended with chicory—sometimes in ratios as high as 50:50 [1] . This unique composition gives the beverage its strong, distinctive taste.

Indonesia is a major coffee-producing origin made up of an island archipelago, best known for coffees from Sumatra, Java, Sulawesi, Bali, and Papua. [1] In coffee usage, the term refers to the country’s origin profile: often low-acid, full-bodied coffees, especially those processed with Indonesia’s characteristic wet-hulling method. [2] Indonesia is one of the world’s largest coffee-producing countries, with annual production commonly reported in the roughly 10–12 million 60-kilogram bag range in recent USDA/FAS reporting. [3]

Inka is a Polish roasted grain beverage and brand. Developed in the late 1960s during communist rule, Inka has been produced in Skawina since 1971, a centre of coffee production since the early 20th century. Presently it is manufactured by GRANA Sp. Z O.O. While it was used in part as a coffee substitute to alleviate coffee shortages in the 1970s, Inka remains popular, in part to the fact that it is caffeine-free.

Instant taste describes the distinctive sensory profile of instant coffee, characterized by a concentrated flavor that differs from traditionally brewed coffee. [1] The taste results from the extraction process where coffee grounds undergo pressurized water treatment at 175°C (347°F), producing a concentrated brew containing 25% to 60% extracted soluble compounds. [2] This concentrated extraction creates a flavor profile that tends toward intensity rather than complexity . The sweetness component plays a crucial role in instant coffee’s taste profile. [3]

Ipoh White Coffee is a distinctive Malaysian coffee beverage that originated in the city of Ipoh, located in the state of Perak [1] . This specialty drink differs from conventional coffee through its unique roasting process , where green coffee beans are roasted at lower temperatures between 325°F and 375°F, creating a lighter-colored bean with reduced bitterness [2] .

Irish coffee is a hot coffee cocktail that combines a strong coffee brew, Irish whiskey, sugar, and a layer of cream on top [1] . This beverage is traditionally served in a clear glass mug , which shows its distinct layered appearance valued in coffee presentation [2] . The standard preparation includes approximately 30ml (1oz) of Irish whiskey, though premium versions might use specific varieties such as Jameson 12-year or Redbreast [3] .

Jamaica is a Caribbean island nation and coffee origin, referring broadly to all coffee grown and certified on the island. It is distinct from the protected Jamaica Blue Mountain designation, a specific appellation within the country. That distinction matters because the island’s name is backed by a strictly regulated industry and small production across all grades — a reputation that plays out differently across its three official tiers, each covered below. [1]

James Hoffmann is a British coffee expert, author, and 2007 World Barista Champion whose work has redefined specialty coffee culture. [1] As co-founder of London’s Square Mile Coffee Roasters, he gained global recognition through his YouTube channel and *The World Atlas of Coffee*. [2] This guide translates coffee’s complexities for professionals and enthusiasts alike, blending scientific precision with approachable storytelling. [3]
Joshua Spink is an Irish opera singer and writer. His specialist topics are coffee, food, wellness and culture.

Jura Elektroapparate AG is a Swiss developer and distributor of home appliances , headquartered in Niederbuchsiten, Canton of Solothurn. The company was founded in 1931 by Leo Henzirohs. Formerly, Jura ran its own factory, but outsourced production to outside companies in the 1990s. Jura is currently best known for its fully automatic espresso machines . This core area originated in the early 1980s and is nowadays a main element of the brand image as well as creating most of its sales. The espresso machines are produced by Eugster/Frismag in Romanshorn, which also makes coffee machines for Siemens, Bosch and AEG.

Kahweol is a diterpene molecule found in the beans of Coffea arabica . It is structurally related to cafestol . Recent research suggests that kahweol may have beneficial effects on bone by inhibiting osteoclast differentiation. Another recent study confirmed that kahweol has anti-inflammatory and anti-angiogenic effects, offering a possible mechanism for the association found in epidemiological studies between consumption of unfiltered coffee and decreased risk of cancer .

Kalita is a Japanese coffee equipment manufacturer known for its distinctive pour-over brewing devices, particularly the Kalita Wave dripper. This flat-bottomed dripper features three small holes that regulate water flow and promote even extraction , contributing to a consistent and balanced brew.

Karsk (from Old Norse karskr , meaning vigorous), also known as kask or kaffekask , refers to a traditional Scandinavian cocktail. It consists of strong, hot black coffee and high-proof neutral spirits, typically moonshine or vodka. [1] This warming drink originates from rural Scandinavia and is a type of utilitarian beverage distinct from cream-topped cocktails like Irish coffee . [2] Karsk is known for its unique preparation method, which involves using a coin to measure the balance between coffee and alcohol.

Kent is a historic Arabica coffee cultivar selected in Mysore, India , in the early 20th century from a Typica-type planting. It stands as one of the first commercially distributed coffee varieties with meaningful resistance to coffee leaf rust, a fungal disease that devastated Arabica crops across Asia and Africa in the late 1800s.

Kenya, in coffee terminology, is an origin term for Arabica coffees grown in the East African nation, particularly on the high plateaus surrounding Mount Kenya and the Aberdare Range. [1] It is not a processing method, variety, or brewing style, but rather a benchmark origin celebrated for producing some of the world’s most distinctive, complex, and sought-after coffee profiles. [2]

A kettle, sometimes called a tea kettle or teakettle, is a type of pot, typically metal, specialized for boiling water over a heat source, with a lid, spout and handle, or a small kitchen appliance of similar shape that functions in a self-contained manner. Kettles can be heated either by placing on a stove, or by their own internal electric heating element in the appliance versions.

Keurig, is a North American manufacturer of coffee brewers for both home and commercial use. It is a part of Green Mountain Coffee Roasters , Inc. (GMCR). Keurig is based in Massachusetts. Their best selling products are the single serve coffee machine Keurig, and the coffee capsules for the brewer.

A kitchen is a room or part of a room used for cooking and food preparation. In the West, a modern residential kitchen is typically equipped with a stove , a sink with hot and cold running water, a refrigerator and kitchen cabinets arranged according to a modular design. Many households have a microwave oven, a dishwasher and other electric appliances.

KitchenAid is an American home appliance brand owned by Whirlpool Corporation. The company was started in 1919 by The Hobart Corporation to produce stand mixers; the “H-5” was the first model introduced. The company faced stiff competition as rivals moved into this emerging market, and introduced its trademarked silhouette in the 1930s with the model “K”, the work of designer Egmont Arens.

Kopi Tubruk (from the Javanese word for ‘collision’) is a traditional Indonesian coffee brewing method where coarsely or medium-ground coffee is steeped directly in hot water without filtration . [1] It is an unfiltered immersion brew, similar in concept to a rustic cowboy coffee . The grounds settle at the bottom of the cup, creating a strong, full-bodied beverage often called ‘mud coffee.’ [2]

Krups is a German kitchen appliance manufacturer, named after its founder Robert Krups. It is often confused with the Krupp conglomerate. The company also produces a large variety of household appliances. Krups competes with De’Longhi, Sunbeam, Braun, Russell Hobbs, Bosch and Black & Decker .

Laos is a landlocked Southeast Asian coffee origin, with most of its crop grown on the volcanic Bolaven Plateau in the south. [1] The country runs a dual Arabica and Robusta system, with the latter grown at higher elevations than is typical elsewhere. [2] Laos is gaining recognition for clean, affordable single-origin coffee. [3]

A latte, which translates from Italian as “coffee milk,” is a popular coffee drink built on a foundation of espresso and steamed milk . In English, the word is occasionally misspelled as latté or lattè, with the added accent mark considered a hyperforeignism—an attempt to make the word seem more authentically foreign than it is. Interestingly, the term ‘ Café au lait ’ has historically been used for espresso with milk in Northern Europe and Scandinavia. In the United States, however, that same phrase typically refers to a combination of brewed coffee and steamed milk, highlighting a key regional difference in coffee terminology.

Latte art refers to the decorative patterns created on the surface of a latte by pouring microfoam ( steamed milk with small, fine bubbles) into a shot of espresso [1] . This visual enhancement emerged as baristas sought to add aesthetic appeal to coffee beverages while showing technical skill. The core principles of latte art center around milk texture, pouring technique, and contrast. Properly steamed milk must achieve a glossy, paint-like consistency with small bubbles.

Latte Macchiato refers to a hot milk beverage ‘stained’ with espresso, distinguished by its three-layer presentation [1] . Originating in Italy during the 1980s, it emerged as a response to American-style caffè lattes, designed to emphasize the espresso ‘mark’ more prominently [2] .

Luigi Lavazza S.p.A. is an Italian manufacturer of coffee products. Founded in Turin in 1895 by Luigi Lavazza, it was initially run from a small grocery store at Via San Tommaso 10. The business of Lavazza S.p.A. is currently administered by the third and fourth generation of the Lavazza family.

Lelit, an Italian espresso machine manufacturer founded in 1993 in Casella d’Asolo, specializes in compact yet high-performance home equipment. By incorporating commercial-grade components—PID temperature controllers, stainless steel boilers, and E61 group heads—Lelit achieves professional-level precision in temperature stability and extraction consistency. [1] [2]

Light Roast refers to a coffee roast level achieved by heating beans to an internal temperature of 356°F–401°F, halting before the first crack completes. [1] This approach preserves the bean’s inherent qualities, amplifying origin-specific flavors—floral, fruity, and acidic notes—while maintaining a lighter color, higher acidity, and absence of surface oils. [2]
A long black is a style of coffee, most commonly found in Australia , New Zealand and Brazil. It is now becoming available in the UK, predominantly in London.

Low-density lipoprotein (LDL) is one of the five major groups of lipoproteins, which in order of size, largest to smallest, are chylomicrons, VLDL, IDL, LDL, and HDL, that enable transport of multiple different fat molecules, including cholesterol , within the water around cells and within the water-based bloodstream. Studies have shown that higher levels of type-B LDL particles (as opposed to type-A LDL particles) are associated with health problems, including cardiovascular disease.

Lungo is the name for an espresso beverage made by prolonging the extraction time , compared to the normale , which is the standard extraction for espresso. Lungo is the Italian word for long. A normale takes approximately 25 to 30 seconds to pull, while a lungo can go anywhere from 30 to 50 seconds. The volume of a lungo is about the double of a normale. A solo normale contains about 1 oz. of beverage, while a lungo normale is just shy of 2 oz.

A macchiato is an espresso-based drink made with a single or double shot of espresso, lightly ‘marked’ with steamed milk or foam. Derived from the Italian *caffè macchiato* (‘stained coffee’), its name refers to the espresso’s delicate milk accent. This method softens the espresso’s intensity—mellowing acidity and bitterness—while keeping its bold core, creating a balanced yet potent profile. [1] [2]

Malawi is a coffee origin from the East African country of Malawi, known mainly for washed Arabica grown by smallholders in northern highland regions. [1] In specialty coffee , it is recognized for clean, bright cups with floral, citrus, and stone-fruit character, especially from the Mzuzu/Misuku areas. [2]

Malty describes a coffee flavor characteristic that evokes the taste and aroma of malted grains, particularly those used in brewing beer or making malted milk products. This tasting note presents as a sweet, grain-forward flavor with subtle nutty undertones and a smooth, rounded mouthfeel. It shows a cereal-like sweetness reminiscent of barley malt, wheat, or oats, creating a comforting and familiar taste profile. Coffee with malty characteristics often has a medium body with low to moderate acidity .

A manual espresso machine is a lever-operated device that uses human force to generate the pressure required for espresso extraction, bypassing the need for an electric pump. Originating with the 1948 Gaggia lever machine, it revolutionized espresso-making by introducing high-pressure extraction, which produces the signature crema. [1] [2]

Mark Prince is a leading voice in the online coffee and espresso community. He is the founder and webmaster of the influential websites CoffeeGeek and CoffeeKid . His acknowledged expertise and passion for coffee have made him a sought-after source for interviews with various newspapers, magazines, and radio programs.

A Marocchino refers to a classic Italian coffee drink known for its distinct layered presentation. [1] It consists of a shot of espresso , a layer of cocoa powder, and a topping of milk froth . [2] The drink is served in a small, clear glass to show its structure and has a balanced combination of bitter, sweet, and creamy flavors.

A Mason jar—a glass jar with a screw-on lid—was originally designed for home canning but has become indispensable in coffee preparation, particularly for cold brew. [1] Its simplicity and affordability shine in this method, where coarsely ground coffee steeps in cold water before filtering. [2] The wide mouth simplifies filling and cleaning, while the airtight seal maintains freshness during extended steeping. [3]

Mazagran is a distinctive, refreshing coffee beverage with origins in Algeria. It consists of strong coffee or espresso mixed with an equal portion of cold water. The drink is often sweetened and is known as a historical precursor to modern iced coffee .

Medicinal (Coffee Term) In coffee terminology, “medicinal” refers to the health-promoting bioactive compounds naturally present in coffee beans . Research indicates that moderate coffee consumption (1-5 cups daily) gives beneficial compounds with potential therapeutic effects [1] . These include caffeine (50-400 mg/day), which at appropriate doses helps various physiological functions without triggering adverse effects like anxiety or sleep disturbances that appear at higher intakes (>500 mg/day) [1] .

Medium roast is a coffee roast level achieved when beans reach internal temperatures of 410–428°F (210–220°C), producing a medium brown color and dry surface. [1] It balances the brightness of lighter roasts with the caramelized sweetness of darker roasts, creating a well-rounded profile. [2] Compared to dark roasts, it retains more acidity and floral or fruity notes . [3]

A medium dark roast is a coffee roast level defined by beans that reach a deep brown color with visible surface oil, producing a cup with balanced bittersweet flavors, moderate acidity , and a fuller body . [1] [2]

Melitta is a German-based company selling coffee, paper coffee filters , and coffee makers as part of the Melitta Group, which also has Melitta branches in other countries world-wide. The company is headquartered in Minden, North Rhine-Westphalia. It is named after Melitta Bentz (1873–1950) who founded the company after she invented the drip brew paper coffee filter (German patent granted July 8, 1908). Bentz later ran the company as a family business.

Mellow Coffee Flavor A mellow coffee presents a balanced sensory profile characterized by smoothness and subdued acidity . This flavor profile typically develops in medium roasts, where beans reach internal temperatures of 410°F to 430°F, falling between first and second crack [1] . The resulting cup offers gentle, rounded flavor notes without sharp peaks or valleys in taste perception. Mellow coffees have a soft mouthfeel that coats the palate evenly, creating a sensation often described as silky or velvety.

Melya is a distinctive coffee drink characterized by its simple yet flavorful combination of brewed coffee , honey, and a dusting of cocoa powder [3] . It offers a sweet, rich, and slightly bitter profile, serving as a comforting and dessert-like alternative to traditional black coffee. While its exact origins are debated, its name derives from the French and Spanish word “miel,” meaning honey, highlighting a core ingredient [2] .

Mexico is a coffee origin term for coffee grown in the country of Mexico, especially the shade-grown Arabica produced in its southern highland states. It is known for a mild, clean cup profile with sweet, nutty, and chocolate-like notes, and it is often associated with organic or low-input production systems. [1] As one of the world’s larger coffee-producing countries, Mexico has a long growing tradition that makes it a significant and reliable origin in the global coffee trade. [2]

Microfoam is a smooth, dense emulsion of steamed milk and tiny air bubbles, formed through precise aeration and texturing with an espresso machine’s steam wand. Its velvety, glossy texture—reminiscent of wet paint—sets it apart from frothier or unevenly steamed milk, a distinction critical for specialty coffee . [1] [2]

A milk frother transforms ordinary milk into a luxurious foam by aerating it with tiny air bubbles—a fundamental technique for crafting specialty coffee drinks. These versatile tools exist in multiple forms: handheld electric whisks for convenience, manual pump pitchers for precision, and espresso machine steam wands for professional results. [1] [2]

The name ‘Mocha’ originates from the port city of Al Mokha in Yemen, a major coffee trading hub from the 15th to 17th centuries. [1] [2] This port was the primary gateway for Arabian coffee to reach Europe, establishing Yemen as one of the earliest commercial coffee exporters. [2]

Mocha Java represents the world’s oldest recorded coffee blend, combining beans from Yemen’s port of Mocha (also spelled Mokha) and the Indonesian island of Java [1] . This classic pairing balances the wild, fruity intensity of Yemeni beans with the earthy, full-bodied character of Javanese coffee. The blend originated in the 15th-16th centuries when ships from the Dutch East India Company transported both varieties to European markets [2] .

Invented by Alfonso Bialetti in 1933, the Moka Express revolutionized home coffee brewing with its stovetop design, producing concentrated, espresso-like coffee through steam pressure . [1] [2] Its three-chamber system—comprising a bottom chamber for water, a middle basket for grounds, and an upper chamber for the brew—combines simplicity with efficiency. [3]

The Moka pot, often called a stovetop espresso maker, is a device that brews coffee by forcing hot water, pressurized by steam , through ground coffee. Inventor Luigi De Ponti first patented it for Alfonso Bialetti in 1933. Bialetti Industrie still makes the classic model, known as the “Moka Espresso.” This brewer is especially popular in European and Latin American households and remains a cultural icon of home coffee preparation.

Monsooned Malabar (pronounced MON-soond MAH-luh-bar) is a distinctive Indian coffee processing style, not a separate coffee species or farm brand, produced on the Malabar Coast of India. [1] Its green beans are deliberately exposed to humid monsoon winds in open, ventilated warehouses until they swell, pale in color, and lose much of their acidity. [1]

Mount Kilimanjaro, in the context of coffee, is a regional origin name for Tanzanian Arabica grown on the slopes and surrounding highlands of Africa’s highest mountain in northeastern Tanzania. [1] It marks a specific geographic designation, not a distinct botanical variety or separate product category. [2]

Mr. Coffee is a owned by Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a Jarden Consumer Solutions and is a registered product of Newell Brands . The Mr. Coffee brand manufactures automatic-drip kitchen coffee machines as well as other products.

Mucilage (pronounced MYOO-sih-lij), also known as mucílago in Spanish or mucilagem in Portuguese, is the sticky, pectin-rich inner mesocarp layer of a coffee cherry. [1] It sits between the outer pulp and the parchment surrounding the seed, built largely from pectic substances and soluble sugars. [2]

A mug is a sturdily built type of cup often used for drinking hot beverages, such as coffee , tea, or hot chocolate . Mugs often have handles and hold a larger amount of fluid than other types of cup. Usually a mug holds approximately 12 fluid ounces (350 mL) of liquid; double a tea cup. A mug is a less formal style of drink container and is not usually used in formal place settings, where a teacup or coffee cup is preferred.

A muscle contraction is the activation of tension-generating sites inside a muscle fiber, which makes the muscle shorten or hold its length against force. Contractions are started by signals from motor nerves and drive everything from the rhythmic beating of the heart to the controlled movements of a barista’s hands.

Myanmar is a coffee origin in Southeast Asia, known primarily for Arabica grown in the cool highlands of Shan State and, to a lesser extent, in Mandalay and other upland regions. [1] Though a relatively young specialty origin, it has drawn international attention for smallholder-produced coffees marked by clean sweetness and fruity character. [2]

Myocardial infarction (MI), commonly known as a heart attack, is the irreversible death of heart muscle tissue caused by a prolonged blockage of blood flow to a coronary artery. This blockage typically results from a ruptured atherosclerotic plaque and the subsequent formation of a blood clot. Ischemia first affects the subendocardial region, and tissue begins to die within 15–30 minutes of loss of blood supply. In the context of coffee, the relationship is twofold.

Naranjo (pronounced nah-RAHN-ho) is a canton and coffee-producing region in Costa Rica ‘s Alajuela province, situated within the country’s West Valley coffee zone. [1] In specialty coffee, the name functions as a geographic origin designation for green coffee or origin-labeled lots grown on farms within this administrative district. [2] The area has built its reputation on high-altitude farms, award-winning microlots, and a steady record of international competition wins. [3]

The National Coffee Association (NCA) or (National Coffee Association of U.S.A. , Inc. ), is the main market research, consumer information, and lobbying association for the coffee industry in the United States . Surveys produced by the NCA are widely cited in mainstream media. The association has numerous functions and services that include: Market and scientific research Domestic and international government relations, including lobbying Public relations and education.

Natural Process (also known as dry process or dry-processed coffee) is a coffee processing method in which whole coffee cherries are dried intact, with the fruit left wrapped around the seed until the drying cycle is complete. [1] Unlike washed and honey-style methods, no fruit is removed before drying; instead, the entire cherry is sun-dried over two to four weeks, and the dried husk is removed mechanically once the bean reaches its target moisture content. [2]

Natural rubber, also called India rubber or caoutchouc, is an elastic polymer derived from the latex of the Hevea brasiliensis tree, valued for its resilience and waterproof nature. [1] In coffee, the term carries two distinct meanings. First, it identifies the historical material used for group-head gaskets and seals in espresso machines, particularly the E61 lever design, where its compressibility created a watertight seal under high pressure. [1]

Nescafé is a brand of instant coffee made by Nestlé. It comes in many different product forms. The name is a portmanteau of the words “ Nestlé ” and “café“. Nestlé’s flagship powdered coffee product was introduced in Switzerland on April 1, 1938 after being developed for seven or eight years by Max Morgenthaler.

Nespresso is the brand name of Nestlé Nespresso S.A. , an operating unit of the Nestlé Group based in Lausanne, Switzerland. Nespresso machines brew espresso from coffee capsules, a type of pre-apportioned single-use container of ground coffee and flavorings.

Nestlé S.A. is a Swiss multinational nutritional, snack food, and health-related consumer goods company headquartered in Vevey, Switzerland. It is the largest food company in the world measured by revenues. Nestlé’s products include baby food, bottled water, breakfast cereals, coffee, confectionery, dairy products, ice cream, pet foods and snacks.

Neutral flavor serves as the reference point against which coffee professionals evaluate all other taste characteristics. This baseline represents a clean, balanced cup with no dominant flavor notes – neither overly acidic nor bitter, without pronounced sweetness or astringency . Professional tasters use neutral coffee as their calibration standard before evaluating samples with distinct regional or processing characteristics. The neutral cup has subtle grain-like or nutty undertones without sharp edges or overwhelming intensity.

New Orleans refers to a distinct regional coffee culture centered on blending roasted coffee with chicory root and serving it as café au lait with hot milk. [1] The tradition emerged in the nineteenth century when Civil War blockades cut off coffee imports, prompting roasters to stretch scarce beans with the locally abundant root—a practice that stuck as a matter of taste. [2]

Nicaragua is a Central American coffee origin defined by high-grown, washed-processed Arabica production concentrated in its northern highlands. [1] Its coffee matters because it delivers a reliable, easy-drinking profile of sweet chocolate, caramel, and nut flavors, making it a staple for espresso blends and medium-roast single origins. [2]

Nitro Cold Brew blends cold brew coffee with nitrogen gas, dispensed through a stout-style faucet to produce its iconic cascading effect and creamy head—reminiscent of stout beer. The nitrogen infusion imparts a velvety, smooth mouthfeel while naturally amplifying sweetness, eliminating the need for milk or sugar. [1]

Normale, in the context of espresso, is the standard way of extracting a shot. A single shot normale is obtained by extracting approximately 1 oz of coffee, using 7 grams of ground coffee. A single is often named solo, using the Italian word for it. A normale is the standard espresso concentration , whereas ristretto is a concentrated version, and lungo is the diluted version of it.

Nose in coffee tasting refers to the systematic evaluation of coffee aroma during the cupping process, representing a critical stage in professional coffee assessment. This evaluation occurs after the initial fragrance assessment of dry grounds. The process begins when boiled water is added to the coffee grounds, which are then allowed to steep for 4 minutes.

Nutty flavor in coffee represents one of the most recognizable and beloved taste profiles, characterized by distinct notes reminiscent of almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts, or pecans. This sensory experience typically shows as a warm, rich undertone that adds depth and complexity to the cup without overwhelming other flavor components.

Oliang ( โอเลี้ยง ), also known as Thai iced coffee , is a popular and distinctive coffee beverage from Thailand. [1] It is characterized by its unique blend of robusta coffee beans roasted together with grains like corn and soybeans, and often spices like cardamom or star anise, resulting in a deeply aromatic, nutty, smoky, and strong brew . [2]

Oniony in Coffee Definition and Sensory Profile “Oniony” refers to an off-flavor in coffee characterized by distinct allium notes reminiscent of raw or cooked onions. This defect has a sharp, pungent aroma that can range from subtle to overwhelming, often accompanied by a savory, sulfurous taste that lingers unpleasantly on the palate. The onion character typically emerges during cupping evaluation as the coffee cools, becoming more pronounced at lower temperatures (room temperature ) than when hot (~70°C) [1] .

Osteoporosis is a skeletal disease characterized by reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and deterioration of bone microarchitecture, including trabecular bone loss. This leads to compromised bone tensile strength, mineralization, and repair processes due to reduced collagen type I and an altered ratio of non-collagenous proteins to collagen. The consequence is an increased risk of fracture from minor impacts or falls.

An over pressure valve (OPV) is a one-way vent installed in coffee packaging to release carbon dioxide emitted by freshly roasted beans while blocking oxygen ingress. As coffee degasses post-roast, CO₂ buildup can inflate or rupture bags without a controlled escape. The OPV ensures package integrity by allowing gas to exit while maintaining a sealed environment. [1] [2]

Oxidation is the chemical reaction between oxygen and the volatile compounds in roasted coffee, altering its flavor and aroma over time. This process begins immediately after roasting as the beans release carbon dioxide and interact with air, breaking down the delicate oils and organic compounds responsible for coffee’s complex taste. [1] [2]

Oxo Good Grips, a product line by OXO, specializes in ergonomic kitchen tools featuring soft, non-slip handles and user-friendly designs. Within the coffee realm, the brand provides precision tools such as gooseneck kettles, scales, and frothing pitchers, essential for achieving consistency in brewing and milk texturing. [1]

Pacamara is a hybrid coffee variety developed in El Salvador in 1958 by crossing the Bourbon-derived Pacas variety with the Typica-derived Maragogype. [1] The resulting plant inherits Maragogype’s famously large beans while retaining Pacas’s compact tree structure and higher yield potential. [2] This combination makes Pacamara one of the few varieties where bean size directly correlates with cup quality, as the oversized seeds often produce a dense, sugar-rich center cut. [3]

Pacas is a natural, dwarf-mutation variety of the Bourbon coffee cultivar, first identified in El Salvador in the 1950s. [1] This genetic anomaly, found on the Pacas family farm, shortens the plant’s internodes, giving it a compact stature that permits denser planting and easier harvesting. [1] That structural trait makes it a high-yielding, economically vital crop for Salvadoran producers, especially on small farms where space is tight. [1]

Panama is a Central American coffee origin, not a variety or processing method, celebrated for high-grown Arabica from the western highlands of Chiriquí province. [1] Its farms cluster around Boquete, Volcán, and Renacimiento, with Boquete on the slopes of Volcán Barú as the best-known district.

A Panarello steam wand is a frothing attachment for home espresso machines, featuring a plastic sleeve that fits over a standard steam wand. Its built-in air-intake hole automatically aerates milk, simplifying microfoam creation for beginners. Unlike traditional steam wands, it mechanically introduces air, producing consistently thick foam with minimal skill. [1] [2] [3]

Paper filters are thin, disposable sheets of porous paper designed to hold ground coffee while allowing water to pass through. Patented by Melitta Bentz in 1908, they are essential for pour-over drippers and automatic coffee makers. [1] By trapping fine particles and oils, they produce a clean, sediment-free cup with bright clarity, enhancing delicate flavors in light to medium roasts. [2]

Papery flavor represents a negative taste descriptor for coffee, characterized by a dry, thin, and flat taste reminiscent of wet paper or cardboard [1] . This unwanted sensory profile creates an unpleasant drinking experience that masks the coffee’s intended flavor characteristics. Coffee professionals categorize papery flavor as a type of ‘ taint ‘ or ‘off-flavor’ related to staleness and oxidation , rather than a roast defect or inherent bean characteristic [1] .

Papua New Guinea is a coffee-producing country in the western Pacific and a distinctive coffee origin whose highland Arabica grows in remote, rugged terrain. [1] Its highland terroir shapes the origin more than any single roast profile, and around 95% of its coffee is Arabica. [2] The cups come out clean and sweet, with a medium-to-full body and flavors that can range from citrus and tropical fruit to cocoa and mild earthiness. [3]
Past crop refers to coffee beans from a harvest that is more than 12 months past its harvest date, having undergone significant physical and chemical changes due to prolonged storage. [1]

Peaberry Coffee was a coffee shop chain that was started in Denver , Colorado in 1990 by Bill Tointon. The store’s concept was founded on serving a variety of coffee from all over the world and roasting it in Denver. It was categorized in a menu format called the “Peaberry Profile System”. The system offered four selections of coffee roasting styles, Light & Mild, Rich & Creamy, Extravagant & Exotic and Dark & Intense.

Peasy refers to a specific off-flavor in coffee characterized by distinct vegetal notes reminiscent of raw green peas or bell peppers [1] . This undesirable taste attribute typically manifests when coffee has been under-roasted or when beans have not fully developed during the roasting process before reaching pyrolysis at approximately 465°F (240°C) [2] . In sensory evaluation, peasy notes present a sharp, somewhat astringent mouthfeel accompanied by a lingering aftertaste that lacks sweetness.

Caro, sold as Pero in the United States, is a caffeine-free roasted grain beverage made by Nestlé from roasted barley, malted barley, rye and chicory. [1] The drink was first introduced in West Germany in 1954 as a coffee substitute .

Peru sits on the eastern slopes of the Andes in South America, producing washed Arabica beans at high altitudes on smallholder farms. [1] That geography and processing method deliver cups that are clean, mild, and sweet, with a gentle acidity that makes them exceptionally approachable. [2]

Koninklijke Philips Electronics N.V. (Royal Philips Electronics, commonly known as Philips) is a Dutch multinational electronics company headquartered in Amsterdam. It was founded in Eindhoven in 1891 by Gerard Philips and his father Frederik. It is one of the largest electronics companies in the world and employs around 122,000 people across more than 60 countries.

The phin (phin cà phê, pronounced “feen”) is a small, stamped-metal coffee brewer that sits directly on a cup or glass, brewing by gravity alone. [1] It is a distinct brewing device and method, not a finished beverage. As the traditional tool behind Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê sữa đá), it extracts dark-roast robusta one slow bead at a time. [1]

In the coffee maker industry, a PID controller improves brewing precision by keeping the water temperature within a tight, desired range. This is especially critical for espresso, where even a few degrees can change a shot from perfectly balanced to unpleasantly sour or bitter . By replacing older, less responsive thermostats, the PID brings a level of temperature control once found only in professional machines to a wider market, directly impacting the quality and consistency of the final cup.

Generally, plastic is best avoided in coffee making equipment, particularly for components that touch hot water. While BPA is widely recognized as a health concern when consumed in significant amounts, other chemical compounds used in plastic production can present greater risks, though they are less familiar to the public. Heat can accelerate the transfer of these substances from the plastic into the beverage, a process known as leaching. For this reason, materials like stainless steel, glass, or certified ceramics are often recommended for hot brewing stages to ensure purity and safety.

A plunger, or French press, is a manual brewing device featuring a cylindrical carafe and a plunger equipped with a metal mesh filter. Coffee grounds steep in hot water, and the plunger separates them to produce a full-bodied brew. This immersion method extracts rich flavors and retains natural oils, unlike paper-filtered methods, through direct contact between water and coffee. [1] [2]

A pod coffee machine brews single servings using pre-portioned, sealed capsules of ground coffee, delivering speed and consistency in every cup. Pioneered in the 1980s by brands like Nespresso and Keurig, these systems transformed home brewing by replacing manual measurements with unmatched convenience. [1] [2] The airtight pods keep coffee fresh while ensuring uniform extraction, though some purists critique the lack of customization. [3]

Polycarbonate is a high-performance thermoplastic polymer known for its strength, clarity, and heat resistance Wikipedia . In coffee gear, it is valued for its thermal insulation, which is known for trapping heat up to 60% better than glass Acme Plastics . Its softening temperature can range from 150–160°C, while its glass transition temperature is approximately 145–150°C, ensuring durability and clarity at typical coffee-serving temperatures Merriam-Webster . Polycarbonate’s lightweight and impact-resistant properties make it ideal for travel mugs, French presses, and other coffee accessories. Its transparency is similar to glass, while its resistance to thermal stress plays a role in preventing cracks under rapid temperature changes, making it a reliable choice for both hot and cold beverages.

Porcelain is a preferred material for many coffee-making items, such as mugs , cups, drippers, kettles, and pots. Its widespread use comes from its unique qualities, which result from a special recipe and a precise making process. Although it is part of the larger ceramic family, porcelain is often seen as a premium choice. It can replace other ceramics for numerous tasks because it is more durable and has a finer, more elegant look.

A portafilter (or group handle) attaches to the grouphead of semi-automatic and piston-driven espresso machines , and carries a tamped puck of coffee grounds within its basket. It is usually made of brass for better heat retention, but often is made of aluminium to save costs. The portafilter is attached to a plastic or wooden handle.

Postum is a powdered roasted grain beverage often used as a coffee substitute . The caffeine-free beverage was created by Post Cereal Company founder C. W. Post in 1895 and marketed as a healthful alternative to coffee. (The Postum Cereal Company eventually became General Foods, which was bought by Kraft Foods. ) Post was a student of John Harvey Kellogg, who believed caffeine to be unhealthy. The “instant” drink mix version was developed in 1912, replacing the original brewed beverage.

Pour over coffee is a manual brewing method where hot water is poured over coffee grounds in a filter, allowing the brewed coffee to drip into a vessel below. The technique uses a controlled, circular pouring motion to ensure even extraction of flavors. It uses a grind size ranging from medium to fine, which is finer than French press but coarser than espresso, influencing extraction rate and flow.

Pre-infusion is the initial phase of espresso extraction where water is gently introduced to the coffee puck at low pressure (typically 1-3 bars) before full brewing pressure is applied. This technique, rooted in traditional lever espresso machines, serves two critical functions: it evenly hydrates the coffee grounds, allowing them to expand and release trapped gases, while simultaneously preventing channeling by eliminating dry pockets. [1]

Pressure is the ratio of force to the area over which that force is distributed. Pressure is force per unit area applied in a direction perpendicular to the surface of an object. Gauge pressure (also spelled gage pressure) is the pressure relative to the local atmospheric or ambient pressure. While pressure may be measured in any unit of force divided by any unit of area, the SI unit of pressure is called the pascal (Pa) after the seventeenth-century philosopher and scientist Blaise Pascal.

A pressure gauge is an instrument on an espresso machine that measures the water pressure applied to the coffee puck during extraction, typically displayed in bars or PSI (pounds per square inch). It ensures consistent espresso quality by monitoring the ideal 9-bar range, the standard for optimal extraction, preventing under-extraction or over-extraction. [1] [2]

Pressure profiling involves the controlled variation of water pressure during espresso extraction, adjusted in real time by the barista or programmed into an espresso machine. Unlike traditional espresso brewing, which has a steady pressure of around 9 bars, this technique enables precise manipulation of the extraction process, influencing variables like flow rate and contact time. [1]

A pressurized basket is a specialized portafilter basket designed to create artificial pressure during espresso extraction through a single, restricted exit hole. Unlike traditional baskets, it works with inconsistent grind size or uneven tamping by forcing water through this narrow opening, producing a crema-like foam. This adaptable design suits entry-level machines and beginners but limits extraction control, yielding less nuanced flavors than non-pressurized alternatives. [1] [2] [3]

Coffee perception centers around five primary taste sensations detected by taste buds on the tongue and palate. Bitterness , the most prominent taste in coffee, results from compounds like caffeine and chlorogenic acids, with intensity varying based on roast level [1] . Sweetness manifests as pleasant, sugar-like notes often found in properly extracted coffees. Sourness ( acidity ) contributes brightness and vibrancy, ranging from crisp citrus to softer malic acid notes.

Puckpuck is a specialized cold drip brewing attachment that converts an AeroPress into a slow-drip cold brew device. It consists of a drip regulator and a stand, enabling precise control over water flow for consistent extraction. By adjusting the drip rate, users can produce a clean, concentrated cold brew with balanced acidity and nuanced flavors, typically over several hours. The attachment’s compact design leverages the AeroPress’s portability, making it a practical option for home brewers seeking café-quality cold brew without bulky equipment. Cold drip brewing minimizes bitterness and astringency by avoiding prolonged immersion, resulting in a smoother, more aromatic cup. The Puckpuck’s affordability and simplicity have made it popular among coffee enthusiasts exploring alternative cold brew methods beyond traditional immersion or toddy systems. [1] [2]

Puerto Rico is a Caribbean coffee origin from the island’s mountainous interior, known for high-grown Arabica beans, especially in the Cordillera Central. [1] It stands out for small-scale production, a famous past, and washed, mountain-grown coffees with a smooth, balanced profile. [2] That tradition once made the island a major global exporter, but today it endures primarily through its own vibrant café culture. [3]

Pulped Natural Process (also known as semi-washed, or cereja descascada in Brazil) is a coffee processing method in which the outer skin of the coffee cherry is mechanically removed soon after harvest, while some or most of the sticky mucilage layer remains attached to the parchment-covered seed during drying. [1] It sits between washed and natural processing, combining the cleaner, more acidic cup profile of a washed coffee with the heavier body and sweetness of a natural, making it a favorite for espresso blends seeking balance. [2] Because the fruit is removed before drying, the coffee is less prone to the over-fermentation and moldy flavors that can plague naturals, yet it still absorbs sugars from the remaining mucilage, enhancing perceived sweetness and roundness. [3] This method is particularly valued in regions with limited water access or unpredictable rainfall, as it requires significantly less water than fully washed processing while producing a more consistent and marketable result than traditional sun-dried naturals. [1] The technique is a cornerstone of Brazilian coffee production , where it was pioneered to balance efficiency with extraction quality. [3]

Quakers are defective coffee beans that create distinct negative sensory characteristics when present in sufficient quantities within a coffee blend. [1] These underdeveloped beans appear lighter in color compared to properly developed coffee beans , often displaying a pale, whitish, or lighter brown appearance that makes them identifiable during visual inspection. [1] The flavor impact of quakers has harsh , astringent, and unpleasantly bitter notes that can overpower the desired flavor characteristics of quality coffee. [2]

Rancid Flavor in Coffee: Definition and Sensory Profile Rancid flavor is a distinct off-note in coffee characterized by unpleasant, fatty, sour qualities reminiscent of spoiled butter or oxidized oils. In sensory evaluation, rancid notes present as a combination of stale, cardboard-like aromas with sour, pungent undertones. The flavor typically intensifies over time as coffee ages, particularly when stored improperly. Research comparing Arabica and Robusta varieties found that both develop rancid characteristics during storage, though at different rates [1] .

Rancilio is an espresso machine manufacturer, founded in 1927 by Roberto Rancilio in Parabiago, Milan, Italy. Rancilio would become best known for its innovative distribution networks, effective use of industrial design and reputable reliability. Rancilio’s earliest well-known machine was ‘La Regina’ – a vertical boiler machine, similar to the original Bezzera and Victoria Arduino devices in function and gilded ‘Belle Epoque’ styling.

The Rancilio Silvia, introduced in 1997 by Italian manufacturer Rancilio, is a semi-automatic espresso machine designed for home use. Featuring commercial-grade components like a brass boiler and sturdy portafilter, it produces café-quality espresso when paired with proper technique and a high-quality grinder. Its durable construction and minimalist design appeal to espresso enthusiasts seeking skill development. [1] [2]

Ready To Drink Coffee (RTD) refers to pre-brewed, packaged coffee beverages made for immediate consumption without extra preparation. These products include cold brews, lattes, nitro coffees, and espresso shots, usually sold in cans, bottles, or cartons. [1] RTD coffee gained popularity in Japan during the 1960s with canned coffee vending machines, later spreading globally as a convenient alternative to freshly brewed coffee. [2] Its appeal lies in portability, consistency, and shelf stability, catering to busy consumers who prioritize speed without compromising quality. [3]

A Red Eye is a coffee beverage that combines drip coffee with a shot of espresso. The standard preparation involves brewing an 8 oz (237 ml) cup of drip coffee using gravity filtration , then adding a 1 oz (30 ml) espresso shot produced under high pressure [1] . This combination gives a significant caffeine boost, typically containing between 160-200 mg of caffeine, though exact amounts vary based on brew strength and shot size [2] .

A review is an evaluation of a publication, product, service, or company such as a movie, video game, musical composition (music review of a composition or recording), book; a piece of hardware like a car, home appliance , or computer; or an event or performance, such as a live music concert, play, musical theater show, or dance show. In addition to a critical evaluation, the review’s author may assign the work a rating to indicate its relative merit.

Ristretto is a short shot of espresso coffee made with the normal amount of ground coffee but extracted with about half the amount of water. Traditionally, a ristretto is extracted using the same amount of coffee grounds and water as a normale , but reducing the time to brew it. The result is a concentrated espresso with a different flavor and taste profile, and slightly lower caffeine content.

Robusta coffee, also known as Coffea canephora or Coffea robusta, is a variety of coffee plant, with its origins in central and western sub-Saharan Africa. It is a species of flowering plant in the Rubiaceae family. Though widely known as Coffea robusta, the plant is scientifically identified as Coffea canephora, which has two main varieties – Robusta and Nganda.

Rubbery Flavor in Coffee: Definition and Sensory Profile Rubbery flavor is an undesirable taste characteristic in coffee that resembles burnt rubber or synthetic materials [1] . This off-flavor indicates quality issues or processing problems in the coffee supply chain. When present, the rubbery notes create an unpleasant sensory experience that masks the coffee’s intended flavor profile.

Ruiru 11 is a compact, high-yielding Arabica coffee variety developed in Kenya and released in 1985 by the Coffee Research Station in Ruiru, which gives the variety its name. Its strong resistance to coffee berry disease (CBD) and tolerance to coffee leaf rust make it a practical choice for farmers facing disease pressure.

Rwanda is an East African coffee origin known for producing high-grown Arabica coffees, particularly the Red Bourbon variety, which are typically fully washed at centralized washing stations. [1] In coffee terminology, “Rwanda” refers to beans from this country rather than a processing method or flavor note. Its coffee sector has become a global benchmark for quality-driven, smallholder-led production. [2]

Saeco International Group S.p.A., or Saeco for short, is an Italian manufacturer of manual, super-automatic and capsule based espresso machines as well other electrical goods, with headquarters and factories in Gaggio Montano, located near Bologna.

The Specialty Coffee Association (SCA) is the non-profit trade organization for the specialty coffee industry. SCA stands for the Specialty Coffee Association, the global body created in 2017 when the Specialty Coffee Association of America (SCAA) and the Specialty Coffee Association of Europe (SCAE) merged. The SCA represents every segment of the industry, including producers, coffee roasters , importers and exporters, retailers, coffee brewing equipment manufacturers, baristas and other industry professionals.

Scorched coffee represents one of the most recognizable roasting defects, occurring when excessive heat application damages coffee beans during the roasting process. This defect shows when roasters apply too much heat quickly, particularly during the early stages, causing the bean’s exterior to burn while the interior remains underdeveloped [1] . The resulting coffee has characteristic burnt, acrid flavors that overpower the bean’s natural characteristics. The phenomenon differs from intentionally dark roasts through its uneven development pattern.

A screen filter is a type of filter using a rigid or flexible screen to separate sand and other fine particles out of water. Typical screen materials include stainless steel , polypropylene, nylon and polyester.

Semi-automatic espresso machines are devices that partially automate the espresso brewing process . Compared with super automatic machines , they require more work and know-how from the barista. They are the choice of coffee shops and espresso aficionados. They offer excellent reliability and control over the brewing process.

Senseo is a registered trademark for a coffee brewing system from Dutch companies Philips and Douwe Egberts. The three main characteristics of the system are its coffee pods (called pads in some countries), its design and its easy to use system.

Sidra is a rare, naturally occurring hybrid coffee variety of the Arabica species, most famously cultivated in Ecuador ’s Pichincha and Loja provinces. [1] Its genetic lineage, likely a cross between Typica and Bourbon, yields an exceptionally complex flavor profile with intense floral notes, bright citrus acidity, and pronounced tropical-fruit sweetness. [2]

Single in the context of espresso brewing , refers to a single shot of espresso , pulled from approximately 7-8 grams of coffee grounds. Also called a solo, by the Italian name, a single shot normale espresso holds about 1 oz. of brewed coffee, and it is prepared using a single filter basket .

Single Origin Coffee refers to coffee from a single geographical region, country, farm, or estate. Unlike blends, single-origin coffees show the distinct characteristics of their specific growing location. The concept gained prominence in specialty coffee circles during the early 2000s as consumers sought greater transparency and connection to coffee sources. Single-origin designations vary in specificity—from broad country labels (Ethiopian, Colombian) to micro-regions, individual farms, or specific plots of land.

A single serve coffee maker is a coffeemaker that can be used to brew a single cup of coffee. The concept of single serve is usually related to automatic drip coffee brewers, since the classic automatic drip coffee machine cannot make small quantities of coffee. Although espresso machines brew a single serve, they are not included in the category. The same with manual coffee brewers.

Single-origin coffee is coffee grown within a single known geographical origin. Sometimes this is a single farm or a specific collection of beans from a single country. The name of the coffee is then usually the place it was grown to whatever degree available. Single-origins are viewed by some as a way to get a specific taste, and some independent coffee shops have found that this gives them a way to add value over large chains.

A siphon brewer is a vacuum-style coffee maker that uses vapor pressure and gravity to cycle water between two chambers—first steeping coffee grounds, then filtering the brewed coffee downward. Developed in the 1830s, this hybrid immersion-and-filtration method achieves precise temperature control , yielding a sediment-free cup with exceptional clarity and aroma. [1] [2]
SL28 is an heirloom Arabica coffee variety selected in Kenya by Scott Agricultural Laboratories in the 1930s, derived from a single-tree selection of the Tanganyika (now Tanzania) variety. [1]

SL34 is a coffee variety developed by Scott Laboratories in Kenya during the 1930s, a Bourbon-lineage selection chosen for its adaptability to high-rainfall conditions. [1] It is the lesser-known sibling of SL28 , yet it carries equal weight in Kenyan coffee production.

Small appliances, also called brown goods (because the color of the wooden and bakelite cases once used) are portable or semi-portable machines, generally used on table-tops, counter-tops, or other platforms, to accomplish a household task. Examples of brown goods are: television and wireless sets; microwave ovens; coffee makers; and personal computers.

Smoothness in coffee represents a harmonious sensory experience characterized by a low-acidity, mellow flavor profile that lacks harshness or bitterness . [1] This quality shows a pleasant mouthfeel—neither thin nor watery—that glides across the palate without astringency . [2] The perception of smoothness emerges when all flavor components integrate seamlessly, with no single element creating jarring sensations. Achieving this balance requires proper brewing conditions, particularly water quality and temperature. Filtered water heated to 195–205°F (90–96°C) helps produce consistently smooth results. [3]

SOLVENT In coffee chemistry, a solvent is a substance that dissolves other materials (solutes) during brewing. Water serves as the primary solvent in coffee preparation , extracting hundreds of compounds that contribute to flavor, aroma, and mouthfeel [1] . The solvent’s effectiveness depends on temperature , contact time , and pressure. In decaffeination processes, various solvents play crucial roles: water alone (Swiss Water Process), supercritical carbon dioxide, ethyl acetate, or methylene chloride. [2] .

Sourness in coffee refers to a bright, sharp, tangy, or tart taste sensation, primarily perceived on the sides of the tongue, and is a fundamental taste attribute distinct from bitterness. [1] This characteristic is central in coffee evaluation. When balanced and pleasant, it is described as “ acidity ” or “ brightness ,” which plays a role in a coffee’s complexity and liveliness.

South America, earlier known simply as America (1507–1538), is a continent located in the Western Hemisphere, mostly in the Southern Hemisphere, with a relatively small portion in the Northern Hemisphere. It is also considered a subcontinent of the Americas. It is bordered on the west by the Pacific Ocean and on the north and east by the Atlantic Ocean; North America and the Caribbean Sea lie to the northwest.

“Specialty coffee” was first used in 1974 by Erna Knutsen in an issue of Tea & Coffee Trade Journal. Knutsen used this term to describe beans of the best flavor which are produced in special microclimates. Specialty coffee is the term commonly used to refer to “gourmet” or “premium” coffee. According to the SCAA, (Specialty Coffee Association of America), coffee which scores 80 points or above on a 100-point scale is graded “specialty.

Spicy notes in coffee represent a diverse category of aromatic and flavor characteristics that add complexity to the cup. On the Specialty Coffee Association ( Specialty Coffee Association (SCA)) Flavor Wheel, spice descriptors appear in multiple sections, including the brown spice family (cinnamon, clove, nutmeg) and pungent spices (black pepper, anise) [1] .

In metallurgy, stainless steel , also known as inox steel or inox from French “inoxydable”, is a steel alloy with a minimum of 10.5% to 11% chromium content by mass. Stainless steel does not readily corrode, rust or stain with water as ordinary steel does, but despite the name it is not fully stain-proof, most notably under low oxygen, high salinity, or poor circulation environments.

Starbucks Corporation is an American global coffee company and coffee house chain based in Seattle, Washington. Starbucks is the largest coffeehouse company in the world, with 20,891 stores in 62 countries, including 13,279 in the United States, 1,324 in Canada, 989 in Japan, 851 in China, 806 in the United Kingdom, 556 in South Korea, 377 in Mexico, 291 in Taiwan, 206 in the Philippines, 171 in Thailand and 10 in India.
Although steam is generally too hot for brewing coffee, the power of steam is used in certain coffee brewing methods to create pressure . Pressure, in turn, improves the extraction .

A steam wand, a stainless steel tube on an espresso machine, uses pressurized steam to heat and aerate milk, creating velvety microfoam. This process relies on precise steam injection and air control, as detailed in the Steam Wand Mechanism and Types section, where tip designs (single or multi-hole) influence steam dispersion and foam texture. [1] [2]

Steamed milk—heated and aerated by an espresso machine ‘s steam wand —has a velvety microfoam with subtle sweetness. The steam heats the milk while forming tiny air bubbles, yielding a smooth texture. Essential for espresso drinks like lattes and cappuccinos, steamed milk softens the espresso’s intensity while adding body and richness. Maintaining the ideal temperature range (140–160°F) preserves milk’s natural sugars without scalding, enhancing specialty coffee . For baristas, mastering this technique is critical—it uses the foundation of crafting balanced coffee drinks. [1] [2]

A Steampunk Coffeemaker is a commercial single-cup brewer that harnesses halogen heating, vacuum pressure, and digital precision to recreate siphon-style extraction. Developed by Alpha Dominche in the early 2010s, this innovative system enables baristas to fine-tune water temperature and agitation with surgical accuracy, yielding a remarkably clean and nuanced cup. [1] [2]

Steeping time—the period coffee grounds soak in water during immersion brewing —is a pivotal variable controlling flavor extraction. It directly governs how much oils, soluble compounds, and aromatic elements dissolve, shaping the brew’s taste, strength, and mouthfeel. Extended steeping increases extraction for bolder intensity, while shorter durations highlight brighter, nuanced flavors. [1] [2]

The stomach is a muscular, hollow, dilated part of the digestion system which functions as an important organ of the digestive tract in some animals, including vertebrates, echinoderms, insects (mid-gut), and molluscs. It is involved in the second phase of digestion, following mastication (chewing). The stomach is located between the esophagus and the small intestine.
