An electric stove or electric range is a stove that converts electrical energy into heat to cook and bake. Stoves are used for coffee preparation in order to heat up water. There are many manual brewing methods that require hot water, but they don’t involve an automated way to do it.

A super-automatic espresso machine performs all or almost all of the coffee brewing automatically. A super automatic espresso machine will automate the following operations that are typically performed manually by the barista:
Surface area is the measurement of the total area (faces or curved surface) of a solid figure.

Taint (pronounced /teɪnt/) is a specific quality defect in coffee, defined as a noticeable but not overwhelming undesirable off- flavor or aroma that falls outside the expected profile. [1] It is a category of sensory defect less severe than a “fault,” which would make the coffee unpalatable. The term is standardized in professional cupping protocols, such as those from the Specialty Coffee Association (SCA), to describe aromatic off-flavors that are perceptible but not overpowering. [2]

Takeya, a Japanese brand renowned for its cold brew coffee makers, focuses on its signature airtight pitcher featuring a fine-mesh infuser for steeping coarsely ground coffee in cold water. Designed for home use, the pitcher’s BPA-free Tritan construction and leak-proof seal streamline the process of creating smooth , low-acid cold brew over 12 to 24 hours. [1] [2]

A tamper is a device used for compacting the coffee grounds when brewing espresso . The “ tamping ” operation is one of the most important steps in espresso brewing. During tamping, the coffee grounds are pressed in to the filter basket , compacting them into a puck. The coffee needs to be compacted in order to create enough pressure for a correct extraction during shot pulling.

Tanzania stands out among East African origins for its dual-crop structure, producing both washed Arabica and unwashed Robusta , with the former dominating export value. [1] The country’s coffee identity hinges on the stark contrast between its northern and southern highlands, each yielding distinct cup profiles. [2]

Tarrazú (also spelled Tarrazu without the accent in international trade) is a coffee origin and legally protected denomination of origin from the highlands of southern Costa Rica, centered on the cantons of Tarrazú, Dota, and León Cortés. [1] High-grown Arabica cultivated between roughly 1,200 and 1,900 meters on Pacific-facing slopes yields a bright, aromatic cup with crisp citric acidity and a clean finish. [2]

The Tassimo Hot Beverage System is a consumer coffee machine that prepares one-cup servings of espresso, regular coffee, tea, hot chocolate , and various other coffee drinks, notably those including milk such as latte or cappuccino . It was first introduced in France in 2004 and is now also available in Andorra, Austria, Canada, Czech Republic, Greece, Germany, Norway, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Russia, Poland, Portugal, the United Kingdom and the United States.

Taste, gustatory perception, or gustation is one of the five traditional senses. Taste is the sensation produced when a substance in the mouth reacts chemically with receptors of taste buds. Taste, along with smell and trigeminal nerve stimulation (which also handles touch for texture, also pain, and temperature ), determines flavors, the sensory impressions of food or other substances.

Technivorm is a Dutch coffeemaker manufacturer. Technivorm manufactures the Moccamaster, one of the few coffee makers approved by the SCAA . They also manufacture coffee grinders , but they are most known for their flagship product the Moccamaster.

Temperature control is a process in which change of temperature of a space (and objects collectively there within) is measured or otherwise detected, and the passage of heat energy into or out of the space is adjusted to achieve a desired average temperature.

Temperature surfing is a manual technique used to stabilize brew temperature on home espresso machines with cycling thermostats. This method involves timing extraction to coincide with a specific phase in the heating cycle, addressing temperature fluctuations common in lower-cost machines like the Rancilio Silvia. Precise temperature control is critical for even extraction and balanced flavor. [1] [2]

Terroir refers to the environmental factors—such as geography, geology, and climate—that, along with a plant’s genetics, give agricultural products their distinctive character. In coffee, the term refers to the holistic expression of a farm’s unique location. This includes altitude, soil composition, rainfall patterns, temperature swings, and local biodiversity. For coffee professionals and enthusiasts, understanding terroir is key to appreciating why coffees from different regions taste so distinct. A high-altitude farm in Ethiopia’s Yirgacheffe region, with its volcanic soil and specific microclimate, will produce coffee with dramatically different flavor notes—like jasmine and bergamot—compared to a lower-altitude Brazilian farm with its richer soil, which often yields nutty, chocolatey profiles.

Thailand is a coffee-producing country in Southeast Asia and a growing coffee origin, with most of its Arabica grown in the northern highlands around Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai. [1] The country splits neatly in two: cool mountainous Arabica in the north, warm lowland Robusta in the south. [2]

Glassware in coffee brewing equipment is exposed to thermal shock when hot water, or coffee is poured into glass beakers, carafes, or other recipients. In order to solve the problem with glass cracking, manufacturers use borosilicate glass , which is resistant to thermal shocks.

A thermoblock is a compact, on-demand heating element in espresso machines, where water flows through internal channels of a heated metal block—typically aluminum or stainless steel . Unlike traditional boilers, thermoblocks heat water instantly during flow, eliminating warm-up delays and reducing energy consumption. This efficiency enables smaller, cost-effective machines, fueling their dominance in home espresso setups. [1] [2]

A thermocoil is a heating system in espresso machines where water flows through a coiled metal tube heated by an internal electric element. Unlike traditional boilers that store and heat larger water volumes, it heats water on demand, reducing warm-up time while maintaining precise temperature control. This design enhances energy efficiency and minimizes temperature fluctuations, crucial for balanced espresso flavor. [1] [2]
The thermostat is a key component of coffee brewing equipment. It is used to ensure coffee is brewed properly, and the extraction is optimal.

Timers are used in coffee makers for various applications. The most common applications are: timing the brewing , starting the coffee maker, or turning it off, timing coffee grinders, as a way to measure the amount of coffee beans used, timing the extraction as a way of controlling the brewed coffee volume.

Tobacco notes in coffee describe a complex flavor profile in the brew, characterized by earthy, woody, and somewhat smoky characteristics that resemble the aroma of dried tobacco leaves. These notes typically present as dry, leathery sensations on the palate, often in darker roasts, accompanied by subtle hints of cedar or hay. The flavor shows most prominently in the coffee’s finish, leaving a lingering impression similar to the scent of a tobacco pouch after extraction .

Toddy is a cold brew coffee concentrate created by steeping coarse coffee grounds in cold water for 12–24 hours using the Toddy® immersion system, developed by Todd Simpson in the 1960s. [1] This slow extraction yields a smooth, low-acid concentrate with minimal bitterness , ideal for mixing with water or milk or as a base for other drinks. [2]

Total Dissolved Solids (often abbreviated TDS) is a measure of the combined content of all inorganic and organic substances contained in a liquid in: molecular, ionized or micro-granular suspended form. Generally the operational definition is that the solids must be small enough to survive filtration through a sieve the size of two micrometer. Total dissolved solids are normally discussed only for freshwater systems, as salinity comprises some of the ions constituting the definition of TDS.

Triple, in the context of espresso brewing , refers to a triple shot of espresso, pulled from approximately 21 grams of coffee grounds. The triple is pulled using special filter baskets that can hold the necessary 21 grams of coffee. Triplo, as is also called with the Italian name, is not just simply a time and volume adjustment variant of the solo. The triple shot needs to be pulled in about the same time as a single. For this, the grind size needs to be adjusted accordingly.

Turkish coffee is a method of preparing coffee. This coffee brewing method is found in the Middle East, North Africa, the Caucasus, and the Balkans. Although the method is named the same, the recipe has slight variations that modify the grind size , the extraction time , temperature, and the concentration .

Typica is a botanical variety of * Coffea arabica * and, alongside Bourbon , one of the two foundational varieties from which most classic coffee cultivars descend. [1] It originated in the highlands of southwestern Ethiopia and spread through colonial trade routes, becoming the first widely cultivated arabica type in the Americas and Asia. [2]

Uganda is one of the few origins where both Robusta and Arabica thrive as native crops. Robusta, indigenous to the Lake Victoria basin’s lowlands, anchors national output with heavy-bodied, earthy, often bittersweet cups that stabilize commercial blends. [1]

The United States is a major coffee-consuming nation whose domestic market and culture have disproportionately shaped global coffee trends, despite producing negligible volumes of its own coffee. [1] Its significance stems from its role as the world’s largest economy for coffee retail, where successive waves of consumption—from diner-style drip coffee to the second-wave espresso boom and third-wave specialty focus—have defined international drink standards. [1]

In the coffee maker industry there are many devices that are equipped with a valve. The use of a valve is different though from a coffee brewing method to another. Immersion coffee makers such as coffee drippers, use a valve to control the steeping time . A simple valve is often found on automatic drip coffee machines as a way to temporarily stop the dripping for pouring a cup.

Vibration refers to a mechanical phenomenon involving oscillations about an equilibrium point. The motion is calibrated by frequency and amplitude to match specific bean size profiles, enabling processes such as specific gravity separation and density-based bean separation.
A Vienna roast is a medium-dark roast level, darker than an American roast but lighter than Full City or French roast.

Vietnam is the world’s second-largest coffee producer and the dominant source of Robusta , a species thriving in its lowland tropical climate. [1] The sector is defined by the Central Highlands, a plateau region where over 90 percent of national output originates, with provinces like Dak Lak and Lam Dong leading cultivation. [1]

Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê đá) is a distinctive cold coffee beverage characterized by its bold flavor profile and layered presentation. This drink typically consists of strong, dark-roasted coffee—traditionally made with robusta beans —combined with sweetened condensed milk and poured over ice. [1] Visually, Vietnamese iced coffee presents as a striking two-toned beverage when unmixed, with the thick white condensed milk layer beneath the dark coffee. Once stirred, it transforms into a caramel-colored drink. [1]

In chemistry and physics, volatility is the tendency of a substance to vaporize. Volatility is directly related to a substance’s vapor pressure. At a given temperature, a substance with higher vapor pressure vaporizes more readily than a substance with a lower vapor pressure.

Washed Process, also known as the wet process or fully washed method, is a coffee processing technique in which the cherry skin and most or all of the fruit layers are removed from the seed before drying begins. [1] A fermentation step breaks down the sticky mucilage layer, followed by washing and drying the bean in its protective parchment. [2]

A Washing Station, also known as a wet mill, factory, or beneficio, is a centralized facility where freshly harvested coffee cherries are received and processed into dried parchment coffee. [1] Here, the initial stages of processing—sorting, pulping, fermentation, washing, and drying—physically happen. [2]

Many coffee makers rely on a water tank, or reservoir to supply the machine during brewing. The water tank solution is convenient, makes it possible to move the equipment, and it doesn’t require an expensive installation.

West Valley (Costa Rica), also known as Valle Occidental in Spanish, is a recognized coffee-growing region on the western side of Costa Rica’s Central Valley plateau, northwest of San José. [1] It is one of the eight official coffee regions designated by ICAFE, the country’s coffee institute. [2]

Wet Milling is the coffee post-harvest process—and the physical facility—in which freshly picked coffee cherries are transformed into dried parchment coffee. [1] This stage strips away the cherry’s outer skin and sticky mucilage before the beans are dried for storage. [2]

Wet-Hulling (Giling Basah), pronounced GEE-ling BAH-sah, is a coffee processing method originating in Indonesia. [1] It strips the parchment layer from the coffee bean while still moist, typically at 30–40% moisture content, rather than the 10–12% typical of fully dried parchment coffee. [2] This early removal exposes the green bean to open air and direct sun during final drying. [3]

Wiener Melange (pronounced VEE-ner meh-LAHNJ, from German for “ Viennese blend”) refers to a traditional Austrian coffee beverage . It is a gentler, creamier variation of a cappuccino , distinguished by its use of milder coffee and a balanced ratio of coffee to milk [1] . The drink consists of a shot of espresso or lightly brewed coffee, an equal amount of steamed milk, and is topped with a light milk foam [3] [5] .

Developed in 1954 by German inventor Gottlob Widmann, the Wigomat revolutionized home brewing as the first fully automatic drip coffee maker. Its design featured an electric heating element, paper filter, and automated drip mechanism, replacing manual pour-over methods while ensuring consistent temperature and extraction for balanced flavor. [1] [2]

Winey Coffee refers to coffee with distinct wine-like characteristics in its flavor profile. This descriptor indicates a cup with bright acidity , fruity notes , and a complex, sometimes fermented quality that resembles wine [1] . The sensory experience includes berry-like flavors (blackberry, blueberry), red fruits (cherry, currant), and occasionally dark grape notes [2] . This profile commonly appears in coffees processed using natural or honey methods, where controlled fermentation develops these distinctive attributes [3] .

Woody Coffee refers to a flavor and aroma characteristic in coffee that is reminiscent of dry wood, oak barrels, or tree bark. [1] This descriptor is complex and can range from a valued note in some premium coffees to an undesirable defect. [2] The distinction depends on whether the woody note is a fresh, intrinsic part of the flavor profile or a stale one resulting from improper storage or excessive aging. [3]

Yemen is a historic coffee origin in the Arabian Peninsula, known for producing small-lot Arabica from highland terraces under dry conditions. [1] In coffee, the term refers to the country’s distinctive origin profile, especially naturally processed, heirloom coffees associated with Mocha and the highlands around Sana’a, Haraz, and Bani Matar. [2]

Yungas (from Aymara for “Warm Lands”) is a coffee-producing region of steep cloud-forest valleys on the eastern slope of the Andes in Bolivia, running from the Altiplano down toward the Amazon basin. [1] It is the country’s historic and principal coffee origin, with plantings between roughly 1,000 and 2,000 meters. [2]
